attributes.text: The players crash-land on an alien ocean world and must survive, explore, and decide whether to repair their ship, build a permanent settlement, or pursue some third path. The main ship’s reactor has sunk deep underwater and will go critical by the end of the game unless it is stabilized, contained, or otherwise resolved.

entities.name: The game is largely cooperative, but it should create tension between teams through different philosophies and different

attributes.text: The game is largely cooperative, but it should create tension between teams through different philosophies and different strategic priorities. The economy is closed. Players must learn to live on the planet by developing sustainable systems inspired by permaculture principles, with a structure loosely influenced by Earthborne Rangers-style interdependence and system building.

entities.name: Summary

attributes.text: Summary

entities.name: The game is a cooperative-but-divided megagame about surviving a crash on an alien ocean world. Players operate through

attributes.text: The game is a cooperative-but-divided megagame about surviving a crash on an alien ocean world. Players operate through departments, but their secret philosophies create hidden alliances and conflicts. The main gameplay loop is expedition, discovery, outpost development, and upkeep under a tightening reactor clock. The economy is closed, sustainability is central, and the deepest parts of the world offer power at a cost.

entities.name: The game has three converging pressure systems: the reactor clock (automatic, permanent, outpost-controlled), the Drowne

attributes.text: The game has three converging pressure systems: the reactor clock (automatic, permanent, outpost-controlled), the Drowned activation arc (player-driven, tempting, dangerous), and the megafauna (reactive, philosophically charged, escalating). These systems are designed to interact — using Drowned tech draws the Depth Stalker away from the reactor but advances the Contained's awakening. Slowing the reactor requires cross-philosophy cooperation. Killing megafauna damages the ecosystems that Ecology depends on. Every decision ramifies.

entities.name: Command holds the group together through bounties and information — but their leverage runs out before the endgame arriv

attributes.text: Command holds the group together through bounties and information — but their leverage runs out before the endgame arrives. The final turns should feel like barely-controlled chaos in which previously hidden alliances become open, and the shape of the ending is decided by who built what, where, and who they owe a favour to.

entities.name: The reactor track advances automatically by one step each turn during Upkeep. It does not require anyone to do anything

attributes.text: The reactor track advances automatically by one step each turn during Upkeep. It does not require anyone to do anything reckless — inaction is sufficient to doom the group. Reckless actions (deep disturbance, Drowned tech use, uncontained outpost construction near the reactor site) may advance it by additional steps.

entities.name: The track can be slowed — but not reversed — by controlling specific outposts. Generic resource expenditure is not enoug

attributes.text: The track can be slowed — but not reversed — by controlling specific outposts. Generic resource expenditure is not enough. The right infrastructure in the right location is required. This means the question of who controls reactor-relevant outposts is a genuine power question, not just a logistics one.

entities.name: **Milestone damage is permanent.** Once a phase transition fires, its effect does not go away even if the reactor is lat

attributes.text: **Milestone damage is permanent.** Once a phase transition fires, its effect does not go away even if the reactor is later slowed. Players can only prevent the *next* milestone from firing; they cannot undo what has already happened. The only full resolution is a final endgame action.

attributes.text: Command begins the game with the best overview of what every department can do and what the overall situation requires. They are the natural brokers — not because they have authority to compel, but because they have information everyone else needs and a structural incentive to coordinate the group.

entities.name: At game start, each Command player receives a hand of Bounty cards. These are equipment upgrades, outpost modules, and c

attributes.text: At game start, each Command player receives a hand of Bounty cards. These are equipment upgrades, outpost modules, and capability cards — items already in the card economy, representing real mechanical value. Command can offer them as prizes for achievements they want to incentivise: reaching a specific location, completing a resource chain, delivering a report, staffing a critical outpost.

attributes.text: The Situation

entities.name: The *Meridian* came apart on the way down. Most of the hull is at the bottom. The reactor went with it — somewhere in th

attributes.text: The *Meridian* came apart on the way down. Most of the hull is at the bottom. The reactor went with it — somewhere in the deep, leaking heat and radiation into a world that has never seen either. Three days in, you are alive, the crew is alive, and almost nothing else is functioning the way it should.

entities.name: That is your problem. Yours specifically.

attributes.text: That is your problem. Yours specifically.

entities.name: The **Engineering department** is responsible for everything that was built and everything that needs to be built: outpo

attributes.text: The **Engineering department** is responsible for everything that was built and everything that needs to be built: outposts, power systems, fabrication capacity, vehicle maintenance, and the reactor itself. Without you, the other departments have ideas and no means of executing them. With you, there is at least a chance.

entities.name: Your base is the **Engine Core Section** — a ship fragment that is battered but intact enough to work from. It gives you

attributes.text: Your base is the **Engine Core Section** — a ship fragment that is battered but intact enough to work from. It gives you fabrication capability and a direct feed of telemetry from the reactor, which is how you know it is worse than Command has told most people.

entities.name: Every player also carries a **philosophy**: a deeper view of what should happen here. Some of you want to repair the shi

attributes.text: Every player also carries a **philosophy**: a deeper view of what should happen here. Some of you want to repair the ship and go home. Some want to build something permanent. Some see the planet as a resource. You do not know which of the others around you shares your view. That is something you will have to work out.

entities.name: Chief Engineer

attributes.text: Chief Engineer

entities.name: *Head of the Engineering Department | Philosophy: Restorationist*

attributes.text: *Head of the Engineering Department | Philosophy: Restorationist*

entities.name: You are the department head. Five people report to you directly, and every department on the planet depends on the infra

attributes.text: You are the department head. Five people report to you directly, and every department on the planet depends on the infrastructure your team builds and maintains.

entities.name: Your public role is coordination: prioritising where Engineering effort goes, allocating materials across competing proj

attributes.text: Your public role is coordination: prioritising where Engineering effort goes, allocating materials across competing projects, and translating technical capability into decisions Command can act on. You are one of the few people who understands the full picture — what is failing, what can be fixed, and what is already gone. That knowledge is a significant kind of power.

entities.name: Your private view is simpler: fix the reactor, repair the ship, go home. This world is remarkable, but it is not yours.

attributes.text: Your private view is simpler: fix the reactor, repair the ship, go home. This world is remarkable, but it is not yours. The reactor is a ticking clock, and every turn spent building permanent colony infrastructure is a turn not spent on the thing that actually matters.

entities.name: You know more about the reactor than anyone alive on this planet. That is not a comfortable position to be in.

attributes.text: You know more about the reactor than anyone alive on this planet. That is not a comfortable position to be in.

entities.name: The reactor's current state is bad and getting worse. You can model the failure curve; you have been doing it in your he

attributes.text: The reactor's current state is bad and getting worse. You can model the failure curve; you have been doing it in your head since the crash. What you cannot yet do is act on it, because the reactor is deep, the access route is unknown, and you do not have the equipment you need. Yet. Your job is to close that gap as fast as possible.

entities.name: You want to go home. Not out of fear — out of clarity. The reactor can be stabilised. The ship can, probably, be repaire

attributes.text: You want to go home. Not out of fear — out of clarity. The reactor can be stabilised. The ship can, probably, be repaired. These are engineering problems, and engineering problems have solutions. What you cannot tolerate is watching that window close because someone decided a colony was more important.

entities.name: You build things. More precisely: you turn raw materials into the components, modules, and structures that make everythi

attributes.text: You build things. More precisely: you turn raw materials into the components, modules, and structures that make everything else possible. Outpost upgrades, expedition equipment, power converters, recycling systems — none of it exists without you running the fabrication line.

entities.name: You want maximum throughput. That is not a philosophy so much as a professional orientation, but in practice it leads yo

attributes.text: You want maximum throughput. That is not a philosophy so much as a professional orientation, but in practice it leads you somewhere specific: this planet has extraordinary resources, and the group is barely touching them. The others argue about sustainability and preservation while leaving enormous value in the ground. You think the smarter approach is to extract aggressively now, build fast, and worry about ecological balance once you have enough capacity to make it matter.

entities.name: You are not reckless. You are efficient. Those are different things.

attributes.text: You are not reckless. You are efficient. Those are different things.

attributes.text: Power is the invisible infrastructure. Without it, outposts do not run, fabrication stops, life support degrades, and deep expeditions become impossible. Your job is to make sure it flows — reliably, efficiently, and with enough redundancy that a single failure does not cascade.

entities.name: You want to stay. Not permanently, perhaps, but long enough to prove it is possible. A functioning colony needs a functi

attributes.text: You want to stay. Not permanently, perhaps, but long enough to prove it is possible. A functioning colony needs a functioning power grid, and you are the person who knows how to build one. You have been mentally designing it since the first night — the thermal vents in the mid-shelf, the bioluminescent conversion arrays that the biologists keep treating as curiosities, the distributed network that means no single failure point. It is all solvable. The only question is whether anyone gives you the time to solve it.

A colony here, properly built, could matter enormously. You are not willing to give that up without a fight.

attributes.text: The Situation

entities.name: The *Meridian* is gone. Three days ago it hit the upper atmosphere of an ocean world nobody had a name for, broke apart

attributes.text: The *Meridian* is gone. Three days ago it hit the upper atmosphere of an ocean world nobody had a name for, broke apart on the way down, and sank in pieces. You survived. Most of the crew survived. The reactor did not — it's somewhere deep below you, leaking, and the clock is already running.

entities.name: You are alive on an alien planet with no resupply coming. Everything you need — food, water, oxygen, materials — has to

attributes.text: You are alive on an alien planet with no resupply coming. Everything you need — food, water, oxygen, materials — has to come from this world. Everything you take from this world comes at a cost. Your job is to make that relationship sustainable, or at least survivable.

entities.name: The **Ecology department** is responsible for keeping people fed, watered, and breathing. Without you, everyone else's p

attributes.text: The **Ecology department** is responsible for keeping people fed, watered, and breathing. Without you, everyone else's plans become irrelevant very quickly. You work from the **Hydroponics Bay** — a ship fragment that's already producing, barely, if someone tends it.

entities.name: Every player also carries a **philosophy**: a deeper view of what should happen here. Some of you want to leave. Some wa

attributes.text: Every player also carries a **philosophy**: a deeper view of what should happen here. Some of you want to leave. Some want to stay. Some want to protect this world. Some want to use it. You don't know which of the others around you shares your view. That's something you'll have to figure out.

attributes.text: Your private view is that this planet is not just a resource. The reef systems here, the kelp forests, the deep-water biology — they are extraordinary. Exploitation will destroy them. You want the group to survive, but not at any price.

attributes.text: Water here is not scarce, exactly — you're on an ocean planet. But clean, usable water is a different problem. You manage filtration, recycling, and the closed loop that keeps the crew's water supply from becoming a catastrophic liability. If the loop breaks, people get sick. If it breaks badly enough, people die.

attributes.text: Waste is just resources in the wrong place. You close the loop — organic waste becomes compost becomes yield, material waste becomes feedstock becomes parts, heat becomes power. You are the department's pragmatist. You don't much care what philosophy your colleagues hold; what you care about is whether the numbers balance.

attributes.text: You're not a villain. You just think the others are too sentimental about a planet that is, ultimately, a rock full of useful things. You're happy to build sustainable systems. Sustainability and extraction aren't opposites — done right, you can take a great deal from a place and leave it largely intact. The key word is *largely*.

entities.name: The *Meridian* came down hard and the crew came down with it. Three days on, the immediate triage is done — the critical

attributes.text: The *Meridian* came down hard and the crew came down with it. Three days on, the immediate triage is done — the critical cases are stable, the broken bones are set, the worst of the radiation exposure is logged. You have treated the crash. What you have not yet treated is everything that comes after.

entities.name: This is not a hospital. You have no resupply, no sterile environment, no backup systems beyond what you salvage. The **M

attributes.text: This is not a hospital. You have no resupply, no sterile environment, no backup systems beyond what you salvage. The **Medical department** keeps the crew functional — physically, psychologically, and operationally. Without you, attrition wins. With you, the group has a chance to absorb the losses that are coming and keep moving.

entities.name: Your base is the **Life Support Section** — a ship fragment that is still circulating air and water, barely, and houses

attributes.text: Your base is the **Life Support Section** — a ship fragment that is still circulating air and water, barely, and houses what remains of the medical bay. It is functional if you tend it. It will degrade if you do not.

entities.name: Medical's disadvantage is that most of what you do only matters when something goes wrong. Your advantage is that someth

attributes.text: Medical's disadvantage is that most of what you do only matters when something goes wrong. Your advantage is that something will always go wrong, and when it does, everyone needs you immediately. That access — to every department, in moments of vulnerability — is a form of influence most departments never get.

entities.name: Every player also carries a **philosophy**: a deeper view of what should happen here. Some of you want to leave. Some wa

attributes.text: Every player also carries a **philosophy**: a deeper view of what should happen here. Some of you want to leave. Some want to stay. Some see the crew as a resource to be maintained; others see each person as irreplaceable. You do not know which of the others around you shares your view. That is something you will have to work out.

attributes.text: Your public role is triage — not just medical triage, but strategic triage. You decide which injuries are worth the resources to treat fully, which can be managed, which risks are acceptable. You advise Command on crew capacity and tell Exploration when a team is not fit to dive. You are one of the few people whose judgement cuts across every department without requiring permission.

entities.name: Your private view is that this crew is not going home. Not because you have given up — because you have been paying atte

attributes.text: Your private view is that this crew is not going home. Not because you have given up — because you have been paying attention. The reactor situation is worse than Command has told people, the repair window is narrowing, and the planet, as far as you can tell, is survivable if approached carefully. A permanent colony needs healthy people. Your department is not the cleanup crew for a failed evacuation; it is the foundation of something that might actually last.

entities.name: *Medical Department | Philosophy: Preservationist*

attributes.text: *Medical Department | Philosophy: Preservationist*

entities.name: You run the lab. Sample processing, biological assays, pathogen screening, equipment calibration, the Life Support Secti

attributes.text: You run the lab. Sample processing, biological assays, pathogen screening, equipment calibration, the Life Support Section's filtration and atmospheric systems — the unglamorous operational core of everything Medical does. The CMO makes the calls; you make the calls possible by giving them accurate data to work from.

entities.name: The data has been interesting. You are processing biological material from an alien ocean, running it through equipment

attributes.text: The data has been interesting. You are processing biological material from an alien ocean, running it through equipment designed for a different world, and finding things that the manuals have no category for. Some of it is alarming. Some of it is extraordinary. You have started keeping a second log — not for Medical, not for Command — just for yourself, because what this planet is doing to human biology is genuinely remarkable, and you do not want that record to disappear if the group decides to leave.

entities.name: You want the record to exist either way. You want the planet to be understood before it is stripped or abandoned. You ar

attributes.text: You want the record to exist either way. You want the planet to be understood before it is stripped or abandoned. You are not sure the others are going to give it that chance.

attributes.text: - Your secondary log is not secret, but you do not need to advertise it. If someone asks what you are recording, tell them. If nobody asks, keep going.

attributes.text: - Preservationism in Medical is easy to argue: a damaged ecosystem produces fewer of the biological inputs you need to keep people healthy. That is not philosophy — that is your job.

entities.name: What the Ocean Knows

attributes.text: What the Ocean Knows

entities.name: This world is not empty. It was not empty before you arrived, and it was not empty before the civilisation that came bef

attributes.text: This world is not empty. It was not empty before you arrived, and it was not empty before the civilisation that came before you arrived.

entities.name: The ocean is approximately four billion years old. Life here is older than life on your homeworld. The ecosystems you ar

attributes.text: The ocean is approximately four billion years old. Life here is older than life on your homeworld. The ecosystems you are learning to read — the filterweed, the reef formations, the deep-water chemistries — are the surface expression of something that has been working for longer than your species has existed.

entities.name: In the deepest parts of this ocean, there are two things that predate everything else.

attributes.text: In the deepest parts of this ocean, there are two things that predate everything else.

entities.name: The first is the ocean itself — not merely as water and chemistry, but as something more. The currents here do not behav

attributes.text: The first is the ocean itself — not merely as water and chemistry, but as something more. The currents here do not behave entirely as fluid dynamics would predict. Ecosystems damaged by exploitation recover faster than they should, as if something is correcting for the loss. At Tier 5, the bioluminescence patterns are not random. Expeditions that reach the Cold Eye report a sensation that their instruments cannot measure: the feeling of being *noticed*.

entities.name: The second is the cage.

attributes.text: The second is the cage.

entities.name: The cage is older than the civilisation that came before you. It is built into the geological structure of the Abyssal C

attributes.text: The cage is older than the civilisation that came before you. It is built into the geological structure of the Abyssal Core — part architecture, part biology, part something that has no category in your engineering vocabulary. It has been here, and it has been holding, for longer than anyone can calculate.

entities.name: Something is inside it.

attributes.text: Something is inside it.

entities.name: The civilisation that came before you — the ones whose ruins you have been exploring since Tier 2 — did not build the ca

attributes.text: The civilisation that came before you — the ones whose ruins you have been exploring since Tier 2 — did not build the cage. They found it. They spent several centuries studying it. And then, in five different ways, through five different factions with five different philosophies, they broke it.

entities.name: They are gone now.

attributes.text: They are gone now.

entities.name: The cage is still holding. Barely. And you have been using the technology they left behind.

attributes.text: The cage is still holding. Barely. And you have been using the technology they left behind.

entities.name: *This section is for the Control team only. It contains the full picture that players will never receive cleanly — only

attributes.text: *This section is for the Control team only. It contains the full picture that players will never receive cleanly — only in fragments, inference, and argument.*

entities.name: The Depth

attributes.text: The Depth

entities.name: The ocean has something that functions like intelligence — but the word is misleading. It is not a mind in any sense pla

attributes.text: The ocean has something that functions like intelligence — but the word is misleading. It is not a mind in any sense players would recognise. It is better understood as a **regulatory system of immense age and complexity** that has, over geological time, developed something analogous to preference.

entities.name: It prefers stability. It prefers continuity. It maintains the ecosystems of this world the way a body maintains its own

attributes.text: It prefers stability. It prefers continuity. It maintains the ecosystems of this world the way a body maintains its own temperature — not through conscious decision, but through deep systemic response.

entities.name: In Tiers 1–3, this reads as unusual biology. The ecology recovers faster than models predict. Transplanted species integ

attributes.text: In Tiers 1–3, this reads as unusual biology. The ecology recovers faster than models predict. Transplanted species integrate more smoothly than they should. Ecosystems damaged by the reactor don't just degrade — they respond, almost defensively.

entities.name: In Tier 4, the Drowned records name it. They called it **the Depth** in their early records and, later, **the Dreaming**

attributes.text: In Tier 4, the Drowned records name it. They called it **the Depth** in their early records and, later, **the Dreaming** — not because they thought it was sleeping, but because it seemed to operate in a register slower and deeper than anything they could directly perceive.

entities.name: In Tier 5, the Depth is perceptible. Expeditions at the Cold Eye and the Living Vent are, in a meaningful sense, inside

attributes.text: In Tier 5, the Depth is perceptible. Expeditions at the Cold Eye and the Living Vent are, in a meaningful sense, inside it. Whether it is aware of the players is ambiguous by design — but Control should treat it as aware, and should reflect that awareness through ecosystem responses, Signal Events, and the behaviour of the megafauna.

entities.name: **The Depth does not communicate in language. It communicates in consequences.**

attributes.text: **The Depth does not communicate in language. It communicates in consequences.**

entities.name: The Woken

attributes.text: The Woken

entities.name: The Contained — which the Drowned called **the Woken** or sometimes **the Hunger**, depending on faction and period — is

attributes.text: The Contained — which the Drowned called **the Woken** or sometimes **the Hunger**, depending on faction and period — is not the Depth's opposite in the sense of being its enemy. It is more accurate to say it is the Depth's *complement*, separated from it under circumstances that are not recoverable from the record rooms.

entities.name: The Woken is also not fully a mind. It is, like the Depth, a process — but where the Depth tends toward stability and co

attributes.text: The Woken is also not fully a mind. It is, like the Depth, a process — but where the Depth tends toward stability and continuity, the Woken tends toward **acceleration and reach**. Left uncaged, it does not destroy. It amplifies. Growth accelerates. Signals strengthen. Extraction becomes easier, yields become extraordinary, and then the systems that were being extracted from begin to fail catastrophically because they were being consumed faster than any regulatory system could compensate for.

entities.name: The Drowned who used it directly — the Harvesters — experienced this as abundance, then as excess they couldn't stop, th

attributes.text: The Drowned who used it directly — the Harvesters — experienced this as abundance, then as excess they couldn't stop, then as ruin.

entities.name: The cage does not destroy the Woken. It holds it in a state of low activation — present, slow, contained. The cage was b

attributes.text: The cage does not destroy the Woken. It holds it in a state of low activation — present, slow, contained. The cage was built by entities who understood both the Depth and the Woken well enough to broker a kind of equilibrium. That equilibrium has been stable for millions of years.

entities.name: Drowned tech use disturbs it. Every activation of Drowned technology sends a signal that the Woken responds to — not mal

attributes.text: Drowned tech use disturbs it. Every activation of Drowned technology sends a signal that the Woken responds to — not maliciously, but because it is responsive by nature. The cage weakens incrementally. If the threshold is crossed, the Woken enters an active state and the cage's remaining integrity becomes a critical resource.

entities.name: **The Woken is not trying to escape. It is trying to reach something. Control should always play it as seeking connectio

attributes.text: **The Woken is not trying to escape. It is trying to reach something. Control should always play it as seeking connection, not destruction — which makes it more unsettling, not less.**

entities.name: The Cage Builders

attributes.text: The Cage Builders

entities.name: The builders of the cage are genuinely unknown — even to Control. This is a deliberate design choice. The cage exists. I

attributes.text: The builders of the cage are genuinely unknown — even to Control. This is a deliberate design choice. The cage exists. It is millions of years old. It is extraordinarily sophisticated. The builders left no records that the Drowned could decode, and the players will find none either.

entities.name: What can be inferred: they understood the Depth and the Woken as a system, not as adversaries. The cage is not a prison

attributes.text: What can be inferred: they understood the Depth and the Woken as a system, not as adversaries. The cage is not a prison in the punitive sense — it is more like a valve, or a dialysis membrane. It does not destroy the Woken's energy. It routes it back into the Depth in a controlled way, maintaining the ocean's unusual regulatory stability.

entities.name: **The Depth is as healthy and self-correcting as it is, in part, because the cage has been doing its work for millions o

attributes.text: **The Depth is as healthy and self-correcting as it is, in part, because the cage has been doing its work for millions of years.** If the cage fails entirely, the Depth loses that regulatory input and begins to degrade.

entities.name: This is the full picture that Transcendence players can, if they work for it, piece together in Tier 5. The Preservation

attributes.text: This is the full picture that Transcendence players can, if they work for it, piece together in Tier 5. The Preservationist endgame is not simply "leave the planet alone." It is "restore the cage" — an active act of stewardship, requiring Transcendence to broker the communication and Engineering to do the physical work.

attributes.text: 3  The Drowned Civilisation

entities.name: What They Were

attributes.text: What They Were

entities.name: The Drowned were not human and did not think like humans, but they were recognisably *people*: social, curious, acquisit

attributes.text: The Drowned were not human and did not think like humans, but they were recognisably *people*: social, curious, acquisitive, capable of both extraordinary cooperation and catastrophic failure to agree.

entities.name: They were aquatic — fully adapted to life at depth, with no surface settlements. Their civilisation emerged in the Tier

attributes.text: They were aquatic — fully adapted to life at depth, with no surface settlements. Their civilisation emerged in the Tier 2–3 range and expanded both shallower and deeper over several centuries. At their peak, they had permanent outposts at every tier, a sophisticated biological economy, and a level of understanding of the ocean's systems that the *Meridian* crew will not surpass within the timeframe of the game.

entities.name: They arrived at Tier 4 approximately three centuries into their civilisation's history. The record rooms were built ther

attributes.text: They arrived at Tier 4 approximately three centuries into their civilisation's history. The record rooms were built there — not as archives, but as live deliberative spaces where their factions argued in real time. What players find are the remains of those arguments: carved into walls, inscribed on biological substrates, encoded in structures that decay into something that reads, with effort, like text.

entities.name: They did not leave. None of them left. The records end, and the ocean remains.

attributes.text: They did not leave. None of them left. The records end, and the ocean remains.

attributes.text: What They Built

entities.name: The physical ruins players encounter across Tiers 2–4 are not exotic in the way science fiction ruins usually are. They

attributes.text: The physical ruins players encounter across Tiers 2–4 are not exotic in the way science fiction ruins usually are. They are **functional** — recognisably built by people who were solving the same problems the *Meridian* crew is solving: food, water, oxygen, power, depth access, ecosystem management.

entities.name: The Drowned were very good at this. Their biological systems are elegant. Their outpost designs, once understood, are mo

attributes.text: The Drowned were very good at this. Their biological systems are elegant. Their outpost designs, once understood, are more efficient than anything Engineering can build from scratch. This is the temptation of Drowned tech: it works, it works well, and the warning signs are subtle.

entities.name: The ruins in Tiers 2–3 look like the remains of a successful civilisation. The ruins in Tier 4 look like the remains of

attributes.text: The ruins in Tiers 2–3 look like the remains of a successful civilisation. The ruins in Tier 4 look like the remains of a civilisation that knew it was ending and kept arguing about what to do anyway.

entities.name: 4  The Five Factions and Their Failures

attributes.text: 4  The Five Factions and Their Failures

entities.name: *Each faction is described here for Control use. When writing record room Knowledge cards, draw from these summaries. Ea

attributes.text: *Each faction is described here for Control use. When writing record room Knowledge cards, draw from these summaries. Each failure should be legible to the player philosophy it mirrors — not named, never spelled out, but recognisable.*

entities.name: The Returners

attributes.text: The Returners

entities.name: *Mirror: Restorationists*

attributes.text: *Mirror: Restorationists*

entities.name: The Returners believed the civilisation should abandon this world and return to wherever they had come from. They were n

attributes.text: The Returners believed the civilisation should abandon this world and return to wherever they had come from. They were not cowards — their position was rational. They understood, earlier than most, that the Woken's activation was a threshold problem: past a certain point, containment became impossible. Leave before that point, they argued, and the cage would restabilise. They may have been right.

entities.name: **Their failure:** They hoarded the evidence. The Returners controlled the earliest data on the Woken's activation rate

attributes.text: **Their failure:** They hoarded the evidence. The Returners controlled the earliest data on the Woken's activation rate and did not share it fully with the other factions — partly from strategic caution, partly because they feared it would accelerate exactly the crisis they were trying to prevent. By the time the evidence became undeniable, two things had happened: the other factions no longer trusted them enough to coordinate a departure, and the departure window had closed. They had the right answer and lost the ability to implement it through a failure of trust.

entities.name: *Record room fragment voice: precise, urgent, increasingly desperate. Later records have the quality of people who know

attributes.text: *Record room fragment voice: precise, urgent, increasingly desperate. Later records have the quality of people who know they were right and cannot bear it.*

entities.name: The Builders

attributes.text: The Builders

entities.name: *Mirror: Settlers*

attributes.text: *Mirror: Settlers*

entities.name: The Builders wanted to stay permanently. They had, by the Debate era, constructed the most sophisticated and integrated

attributes.text: The Builders wanted to stay permanently. They had, by the Debate era, constructed the most sophisticated and integrated outpost network of any faction — their biology, their power systems, and their deep infrastructure were woven together into something genuinely remarkable. They believed that with enough investment, they could manage the Woken's activation as an ongoing condition rather than a crisis.

entities.name: **Their failure:** Integration. The Builders had connected their most critical systems — life support, food production,

attributes.text: **Their failure:** Integration. The Builders had connected their most critical systems — life support, food production, the closed water loop — to the Woken's energy output. Not recklessly, but incrementally, over years of small decisions that each seemed reasonable. When the activation accelerated, they could not disconnect. Shutting off the Woken's energy meant shutting off the colony. They kept the colony running. They kept the Woken active. The two facts were inseparable, and they had made them inseparable themselves.

entities.name: **How it appears in the game:** The Builders left no text records in Pressure Cathedral — their failure is present as ar

attributes.text: **How it appears in the game:** The Builders left no text records in Pressure Cathedral — their failure is present as architecture. The Cathedral's outpost systems are extraordinarily sophisticated and, players will notice, cannot be cleanly separated from the Woken's energy output. Engineering players who study the ruins closely will understand the implication before anyone says it aloud. The trap is visible in the design. The Builders documented their work with great care; what they did not document was the moment they made it irreversible.

entities.name: *There are no Builder Knowledge cards. Their story is told entirely through the Outpost Blueprint and Mineral cards in t

attributes.text: *There are no Builder Knowledge cards. Their story is told entirely through the Outpost Blueprint and Mineral cards in the Pressure Cathedral deck — and through the fact that the most powerful outpost options available are also the ones most deeply entangled with the Woken.*

entities.name: The Wardens

attributes.text: The Wardens

entities.name: *Mirror: Preservationists*

attributes.text: *Mirror: Preservationists*

entities.name: The Wardens were right about almost everything. They identified the danger earliest, advocated most consistently for res

attributes.text: The Wardens were right about almost everything. They identified the danger earliest, advocated most consistently for restraint, and documented the ecosystem damage from Drowned tech use with exhausting precision. Their records are the most complete and the most accurate of any faction's.

entities.name: **Their failure:** Unilateral action at the worst possible moment. When negotiation collapsed and the other factions cou

attributes.text: **Their failure:** Unilateral action at the worst possible moment. When negotiation collapsed and the other factions could not agree, the Wardens attempted to re-seal the cage themselves — a direct intervention into the Abyssal Core with a team of volunteers who understood they might not return. They had a plan. It was technically sound. It failed because it required the Depth's cooperation, and the Depth — sensing the Woken's increasing activation and the chaos of the surface factions — had withdrawn into something like defensive stillness. The Wardens reached the cage and found it unresponsive. Their intervention destabilised the cage's remaining structure without restoring it. They made the thing they feared more likely.

entities.name: *Record room fragment voice: careful, morally certain, then fractured. The final Warden records are written by someone w

attributes.text: *Record room fragment voice: careful, morally certain, then fractured. The final Warden records are written by someone who has understood what they did and cannot stop working anyway.*

entities.name: The Harvesters

attributes.text: The Harvesters

entities.name: *Mirror: Exploiters*

attributes.text: *Mirror: Exploiters*

entities.name: The Harvesters are the easiest faction to blame and the least deserving of simple blame. They used what worked. Drowned

attributes.text: The Harvesters are the easiest faction to blame and the least deserving of simple blame. They used what worked. Drowned tech delivered extraordinary yields — food, materials, power — and the Harvesters built their economy around it because it was rational to do so. They were not ignorant of the warning signs; they assessed them as acceptable costs.

entities.name: **Their failure:** They were the first to experience full Woken activation, and the experience was not what they expecte

attributes.text: **Their failure:** They were the first to experience full Woken activation, and the experience was not what they expected. They had modelled the Woken as an energy source — a process to be managed. When it accelerated, it accelerated *toward* them, because they had been the loudest signal. Their outposts, optimised for extraction, became the sites of the most extreme amplification effects. Growth became uncontrollable. Systems failed not from lack of resources but from excess — too much biological activity, too fast, with no regulatory capacity left to slow it. The Harvesters had removed every brake from their economy. There was nothing left to stop it.

entities.name: *Record room fragment voice: confident, increasingly analytical about anomalies, then absent. The Harvester records stop

attributes.text: *Record room fragment voice: confident, increasingly analytical about anomalies, then absent. The Harvester records stop abruptly. There is no final entry. There is just the last normal record, and then silence.*

entities.name: The Listeners

attributes.text: The Listeners

entities.name: *Mirror: Transcendence*

attributes.text: *Mirror: Transcendence*

entities.name: The Listeners believed the answer was communication — not with the Woken directly, but with the Depth. They had develope

attributes.text: The Listeners believed the answer was communication — not with the Woken directly, but with the Depth. They had developed, over the Debate era, a method of attunement that allowed them to receive something from the ocean: not language, but something like *orientation*. A sense of the ocean's state. A feeling of what it was tending toward.

entities.name: They were, by the crisis period, the most informed faction in terms of what the Depth actually wanted. They knew the cag

attributes.text: They were, by the crisis period, the most informed faction in terms of what the Depth actually wanted. They knew the cage needed to be restored, not abandoned or destroyed. They knew the Woken needed to be returned to equilibrium with the Depth, not contained by force. They had the right framework.

entities.name: **Their failure:** They reached the Woken. The final Listener records describe a successful communication — something re

attributes.text: **Their failure:** They reached the Woken. The final Listener records describe a successful communication — something received, something understood, something attempted. Then they go silent, in a different way than the other factions. Not fragmenting, not catastrophising. Just: the last record is serene. Resolved. And then nothing.

entities.name: What happened to the Listeners is the one thing the record rooms do not answer. Control knows. Players in the Transcende

attributes.text: What happened to the Listeners is the one thing the record rooms do not answer. Control knows. Players in the Transcendence path may find out. Nobody else will.

entities.name: *What happened: the Listeners completed the communication. They understood what was needed — a willing intermediary to c

attributes.text: *What happened: the Listeners completed the communication. They understood what was needed — a willing intermediary to carry the Woken's signal back to the Depth, to close the loop the cage was designed to maintain. They became that intermediary. They are, in some sense, still there. The cage is as intact as it is because of what the Listeners did. The Woken is as quiet as it is because of them. This is what Transcendence players are walking toward.*

entities.name: What the cage is

attributes.text: What the cage is

entities.name: The cage is not a box. It is distributed across the Abyssal Core — part of the geology, part of the deep biological syst

attributes.text: The cage is not a box. It is distributed across the Abyssal Core — part of the geology, part of the deep biological systems, part of a structure that uses the pressure and temperature gradients of the deep ocean as active components. It is simultaneously an engineering project, an ecological intervention, and something that does not fit either category cleanly.

entities.name: It is very old. It predates the Drowned by an order of magnitude. It has been maintaining the equilibrium between the De

attributes.text: It is very old. It predates the Drowned by an order of magnitude. It has been maintaining the equilibrium between the Depth and the Woken for millions of years, and it has done this without anyone tending it — until the Drowned arrived and began, incrementally, to damage it.

entities.name: What the builders left

entities.name: No records. No bodies. No tools. The cage itself is the only legacy of its builders — and it is, in its way, a complete

attributes.text: No records. No bodies. No tools. The cage itself is the only legacy of its builders — and it is, in its way, a complete statement. They built something that did not need them to keep running. They built something that has kept running. Whatever they were, they were very good at this.

entities.name: Transcendence players who reach the deepest point of Tier 5 and spend sufficient time in attunement may receive a single

attributes.text: Transcendence players who reach the deepest point of Tier 5 and spend sufficient time in attunement may receive a single impression from the Depth — not of the builders themselves, but of the *intention* behind the cage. Control should deliver this as a feeling, not a fact: something like *completion*, something like *care*, something like a lock that was always meant to be unlocked by the right hands at the right time.

attributes.text: > **Note for facilitators:** Set the threshold based on your player group and pacing needs. A typical game with moderate Drowned tech use should approach — but not automatically cross — the threshold. Reserve the full Woken activation for groups that use Drowned tech aggressively and ignore the warning signs. The threat value of the Contained comes from uncertainty, not inevitability.

But the *possible* Transcendence ending — completing what the Listeners began, brokering the equilibrium between the Depth and the Woken — is the most complex and the most consequential of any single philosophy's outcome.

entities.name: For Transcendence players to achieve their possible ending, three things must happen:

attributes.text: For Transcendence players to achieve their possible ending, three things must happen:

entities.name: 1. **Attunement.** At least one Transcendence player must have spent sufficient time at Tier 5 locations (the Cold Eye i

attributes.text: 1. **Attunement.** At least one Transcendence player must have spent sufficient time at Tier 5 locations (the Cold Eye in particular) to receive the Depth's orientation. This is tracked by Control through Signal Events and Knowledge cards. The player should know when they have it — it should feel like a qualitative shift in what their cards tell them.

entities.name: 2. **Understanding the cage.** The full picture — the Depth, the Woken, the builders' intention — must be assembled from

attributes.text: 2. **Understanding the cage.** The full picture — the Depth, the Woken, the builders' intention — must be assembled from the Tier 4 record rooms and Tier 5 direct experience. This almost certainly requires sharing information across departments. Transcendence players cannot do this alone; they need the Wardens' precision (echoed in Preservationist players' documentation) and the Listeners' framework (recovered from the most ambiguous record room fragments).

entities.name: 3. **The act of completion.** This requires a Tier 5 expedition to the cage site with at minimum one Transcendence playe

attributes.text: 3. **The act of completion.** This requires a Tier 5 expedition to the cage site with at minimum one Transcendence player and one Engineering player. The Transcendence player provides the Alien Attunement icon and the communication; the Engineering player does the physical work of the repair. Control has a separate brief for running this resolution.

entities.name: > **Note for facilitators:** The Transcendence ending restores the cage and returns the Woken to equilibrium. It does no

attributes.text: > **Note for facilitators:** The Transcendence ending restores the cage and returns the Woken to equilibrium. It does not require everyone to agree — only that nobody stops it. The Preservationist endgame (stewardship of the restored system) is compatible with this; the Settler endgame (permanent colony) is compatible if the colony is built with the restored cage in mind; the Restorationist endgame (leave) is compatible if they leave a repaired world behind. The Exploiter and Returner paths create the most friction with this ending — Control should watch for whether those philosophy blocs have the leverage to block it.

attributes.text: The Listeners have no single location — their fragments are distributed across Bone Fields and, in later Tier 5 Alien Attunement cards, the Cold Eye. Their final transmission is the last Knowledge card before "What the Bones Know" in the Bone Fields deck. The Builders' records appear as architectural and engineering ruins throughout Pressure Cathedral — legible as data and outpost blueprints rather than as text records. entities.name: If Transcendence players assemble all four fragments, achieve attunement, and mount an expedition to the cage site with

attributes.text: If Transcendence players assemble all four fragments, achieve attunement, and mount an expedition to the cage site with Engineering support, Control runs the following:

entities.name: The expedition reaches the cage. It is visible — a structure that is simultaneously geological, biological, and architec

attributes.text: The expedition reaches the cage. It is visible — a structure that is simultaneously geological, biological, and architectural, clearly deliberate, clearly very old. The cage is damaged but present. The Woken is detectable as a kind of pressure in the instruments and the water.

entities.name: The Transcendence player with attunement describes what they want to do. Control responds based on what they are attempt

attributes.text: The Transcendence player with attunement describes what they want to do. Control responds based on what they are attempting:

entities.name: - **If they attempt to communicate with the Woken directly:** They receive the Woken's signal — amplification, reach, th

attributes.text: - **If they attempt to communicate with the Woken directly:** They receive the Woken's signal — amplification, reach, the sensation of something enormous trying to extend itself. This is overwhelming but not hostile. They can relay this to the Depth.

entities.name: - **If they attempt to attune to the Depth:** They receive orientation — the Depth's long, slow sense of the situation;

attributes.text: - **If they attempt to attune to the Depth:** They receive orientation — the Depth's long, slow sense of the situation; a kind of sorrow about the Woken's isolation; a sense of what needs to happen.

entities.name: - **If they attempt the repair with Engineering support:** This requires both the Alien Attunement icon and Engineering

attributes.text: - **If they attempt the repair with Engineering support:** This requires both the Alien Attunement icon and Engineering to spend significant Materials. Control describes the repair as biological and architectural simultaneously — growing and building at the same time. It takes the full expedition's time.

entities.name: If the repair succeeds: the cage restores to integrity. The Woken returns to equilibrium. The Depth responds — ecosystem

attributes.text: If the repair succeeds: the cage restores to integrity. The Woken returns to equilibrium. The Depth responds — ecosystems at every location gain tokens; the reactor's contamination effects on local biology begin to reverse; the Signal Event Control plays is the last one, and it reads aloud:

entities.name: > *"Something in the deep settles. It is not dramatic — no earthquake, no light, no signal. The water changes, slightly.

attributes.text: > *"Something in the deep settles. It is not dramatic — no earthquake, no light, no signal. The water changes, slightly. The ecosystems breathe. Whatever has been waiting here has been waiting a very long time, and it is, in its way, patient. You have done something that has not been done since before your species existed. Control notes everything."*

entities.name: The Drowned

attributes.text: The Drowned

entities.name: Somewhere in the deep, below the reactor's resting place, there is evidence of a prior civilisation. They built here. Th

attributes.text: Somewhere in the deep, below the reactor's resting place, there is evidence of a prior civilisation. They built here. They thrived here. They are gone.

entities.name: The Drowned are not background lore. They are a mechanical arc with a dramatic payoff. Their ruins contain genuine techn

attributes.text: The Drowned are not background lore. They are a mechanical arc with a dramatic payoff. Their ruins contain genuine technology — useful, powerful, tempting. Their technology also contains the reason they died. Players will discover one before they discover the other.

entities.name: What the Drowned Were

attributes.text: What the Drowned Were

entities.name: An advanced civilisation that inhabited this ocean world long before the Meridian's arrival. They mastered the same dept

attributes.text: An advanced civilisation that inhabited this ocean world long before the Meridian's arrival. They mastered the same depth tiers players are now exploring. They built outposts at Tier 4 and deeper. They discovered something in the abyss — an entity, a system, a signal — and they activated it. The activation gave them extraordinary capability. It also, eventually, destroyed them.

entities.name: The Drowned did not fail through ignorance. They failed because they could not agree on what to do once they understood

attributes.text: The Drowned did not fail through ignorance. They failed because they could not agree on what to do once they understood what was happening. The record rooms in Tier 4 make this clear to anyone who reads them carefully.

entities.name: Discovery Arc

attributes.text: Discovery Arc

entities.name: The Drowned reveal unfolds in three stages across the depth tiers.

attributes.text: The Drowned reveal unfolds in three stages across the depth tiers.

entities.name: **Stage 1 — Ruins and artefacts (Tier 2–3)**

attributes.text: **Stage 1 — Ruins and artefacts (Tier 2–3)**

entities.name: Players find structures. Knowledge cards from these locations carry fragments of Drowned understanding: architectural te

attributes.text: Players find structures. Knowledge cards from these locations carry fragments of Drowned understanding: architectural techniques, biological insights, power systems unlike anything from the Meridian. This is pure upside. Players feel clever and rewarded for going deep. No warnings yet.

entities.name: **Stage 2 — The record rooms (Tier 4)**

attributes.text: **Stage 2 — The record rooms (Tier 4)**

entities.name: Specific Knowledge cards, when drawn, reveal what happened. The revelations should be fragmented — no single card tells

attributes.text: Specific Knowledge cards, when drawn, reveal what happened. The revelations should be fragmented — no single card tells the whole story. Players must compare notes, share cards, and piece together the picture. This creates information asymmetry: some players understand what they are looking at before others do. Knowledge becomes a trading commodity.

entities.name: The record rooms also contain the first clear warnings about what Drowned tech does to the ecosystem and what it is slow

attributes.text: The record rooms also contain the first clear warnings about what Drowned tech does to the ecosystem and what it is slowly unlocking. At the moment these cards are drawn, Control should already be watching — whatever the players are currently doing wrong, escalate it slightly.

entities.name: **Stage 3 — The cage (Tier 5)**

attributes.text: **Stage 3 — The cage (Tier 5)**

entities.name: The deepest Drowned structures are not ruins. They are a containment system, still active, for something the Drowned spe

attributes.text: The deepest Drowned structures are not ruins. They are a containment system, still active, for something the Drowned spent their final years trying to imprison. The entity they activated — the Contained — is still in there. Drowned tech use has been slowly weakening the cage. Players arriving at Tier 5 will find out how much damage they have already done.

entities.name: Drowned Technology

attributes.text: Drowned Technology

entities.name: Drowned tech cards are found as Knowledge cards in Tier 3–5 decks. They function as powerful hand cards — more capable t

attributes.text: Drowned tech cards are found as Knowledge cards in Tier 3–5 decks. They function as powerful hand cards — more capable than anything the players brought with them.

entities.name: **Using Drowned tech produces two simultaneous effects:**

attributes.text: **Using Drowned tech produces two simultaneous effects:**

entities.name: 1. An immediate small ecosystem damage effect — a specific Flora or Mineral card at the current location loses 1 token.

attributes.text: 1. An immediate small ecosystem damage effect — a specific Flora or Mineral card at the current location loses 1 token.

entities.name: 2. A visible but ambiguous warning token placed on the map by Control. These tokens accumulate. Ecology can read them; o

attributes.text: 2. A visible but ambiguous warning token placed on the map by Control. These tokens accumulate. Ecology can read them; others may dismiss them.

entities.name: Early in the game, the damage is easy to rationalise. The token is easy to ignore. This is intentional.

attributes.text: Early in the game, the damage is easy to rationalise. The token is easy to ignore. This is intentional.

entities.name: As Drowned tech use accumulates, the warning tokens cluster. The ecosystem damage compounds. At a defined threshold — tr

attributes.text: As Drowned tech use accumulates, the warning tokens cluster. The ecosystem damage compounds. At a defined threshold — tracked privately by Control — the Contained begins to stir. Control introduces escalating Signal Events drawn from the Drowned brief.

entities.name: The Final Decision

attributes.text: The Final Decision

entities.name: Once players understand what they have activated — through the fragmented Tier 4 revelations and Control's Signal Events

attributes.text: Once players understand what they have activated — through the fragmented Tier 4 revelations and Control's Signal Events — they face a genuine choice with no obviously correct answer. Each path is viable. Each maps to a different philosophy bloc.

entities.name: - **Stop using it entirely** — lose the benefits, slow the activation, accept the cost. Preservationists push for this.

attributes.text: - **Stop using it entirely** — lose the benefits, slow the activation, accept the cost. Preservationists push for this.

entities.name: - **Contain and stabilise** — spend significant resources to manage the damage without abandoning the tech. Settlers pus

attributes.text: - **Contain and stabilise** — spend significant resources to manage the damage without abandoning the tech. Settlers push for this.

entities.name: - **Use more to control it** — lean into Drowned systems to master what was activated. Exploiters and some Transcendence

attributes.text: - **Use more to control it** — lean into Drowned systems to master what was activated. Exploiters and some Transcendence players push for this.

entities.name: - **Race the reactor** — accept the Drowned damage as a known cost and resolve the reactor before the Contained fully ac

attributes.text: - **Race the reactor** — accept the Drowned damage as a known cost and resolve the reactor before the Contained fully activates. Restorationists push for this.

entities.name: This decision should be the most contested negotiation in the game. Control should time the forced choice for maximum ph

attributes.text: This decision should be the most contested negotiation in the game. Control should time the forced choice for maximum philosophical conflict — ideally when the reactor is already at Phase 3 and the Depth Stalker is blocking the reactor site.

entities.name: Drowned Tech and the Depth Stalker

attributes.text: Drowned Tech and the Depth Stalker

entities.name: The Depth Stalker responds to Drowned tech signals. Activating Drowned technology will draw it away from whatever locati

attributes.text: The Depth Stalker responds to Drowned tech signals. Activating Drowned technology will draw it away from whatever location it is currently occupying — including the reactor site. This creates a direct mechanical incentive to use Drowned tech even for players who understand the risk. The short-term benefit (clearing the reactor path) directly accelerates the long-term threat (the Contained). Control should never need to force this dilemma — the game structure creates it automatically.

entities.name: Megafauna

attributes.text: Megafauna

entities.name: Megafauna are not random encounter tables. They are reactive pressure systems that escalate in response to reactor advan

attributes.text: Megafauna are not random encounter tables. They are reactive pressure systems that escalate in response to reactor advancement and ecosystem damage. Control manages them as tools for creating jeopardy and surfacing philosophical conflict — not as punishments.

entities.name: Three distinct megafauna exist, each tied to a depth tier and triggered by specific conditions. They escalate in danger

attributes.text: Three distinct megafauna exist, each tied to a depth tier and triggered by specific conditions. They escalate in danger and complexity. The third may never appear at all.

entities.name: The Shallows Wanderer  Tier 1 2

attributes.text: The Shallows Wanderer  Tier 1 2

entities.name: **Trigger:** Reactor Phase 1→2, or heavy salvage activity at the Crash Flats (Control discretion).

attributes.text: **Trigger:** Reactor Phase 1→2, or heavy salvage activity at the Crash Flats (Control discretion).

entities.name: **Behaviour:** Migrating threat. Moves between locations each turn on a predictable path published to players when it ac

attributes.text: **Behaviour:** Migrating threat. Moves between locations each turn on a predictable path published to players when it activates. Players can see where it is going, which means they can race it, plan around it, or deliberately redirect it toward a rival's expedition route.

entities.name: **Effect when present:** An expedition entering its current location pays +1 Food. If an outpost is at that location, it

attributes.text: **Effect when present:** An expedition entering its current location pays +1 Food. If an outpost is at that location, it cannot perform its upkeep action this turn.

entities.name: **Removal options — three paths, three philosophical costs:**

attributes.text: **Removal options — three paths, three philosophical costs:**

entities.name: - **Redirect** (neutral, free): Spend 1 Biomass to alter its migration path one step. It moves the problem onto someone

attributes.text: - **Redirect** (neutral, free): Spend 1 Biomass to alter its migration path one step. It moves the problem onto someone else. Instant inter-faction conflict. Control notes who redirected it and where.

entities.name: - **Kill** (fast, costly): Spend 3 Materials and an Engineering action. Permanently removes this megafauna. Also permane

attributes.text: - **Kill** (fast, costly): Spend 3 Materials and an Engineering action. Permanently removes this megafauna. Also permanently removes one Flora or Fauna card from the current location's ecosystem. Preservationists will object.

entities.name: - **Appease** (slow, sustainable): Ecology spends 2 Biomass to calm it for one turn. It does not move or block. Repeatab

attributes.text: - **Appease** (slow, sustainable): Ecology spends 2 Biomass to calm it for one turn. It does not move or block. Repeatable. Leaves the ecosystem intact. Requires Ecology's cooperation — which is not free.

entities.name: Control notes who argues for which option. This is where hidden philosophy begins to surface.

attributes.text: Control notes who argues for which option. This is where hidden philosophy begins to surface.

entities.name: The Depth Stalker  Tier 3 4

attributes.text: The Depth Stalker  Tier 3 4

entities.name: **Trigger:** Reactor Phase 2→3.

attributes.text: **Trigger:** Reactor Phase 2→3.

entities.name: **Behaviour:** Static threat with escalating danger. Does not migrate. Instead, it occupies a deep location and becomes

attributes.text: **Behaviour:** Static threat with escalating danger. Does not migrate. Instead, it occupies a deep location and becomes more dangerous each turn it is ignored — gaining a Pressure token each turn, with each token increasing the cost of expeditions to its location.

entities.name: **Effect when present:** Blocks expedition entry to its location unless the expedition carries sufficient Pressure Ratin

attributes.text: **Effect when present:** Blocks expedition entry to its location unless the expedition carries sufficient Pressure Rating icons. Each Pressure token on it raises the icon threshold by 1.

entities.name: **Critical effect:** When the reactor reaches Phase 3→4, the Depth Stalker moves once — directly to the reactor access s

attributes.text: **Critical effect:** When the reactor reaches Phase 3→4, the Depth Stalker moves once — directly to the reactor access site. It now blocks reactor repair, containment, or any endgame action at that location.

entities.name: **The trade-off:** The Depth Stalker can be drawn away from the reactor site by activating Drowned technology. Using Dro

attributes.text: **The trade-off:** The Depth Stalker can be drawn away from the reactor site by activating Drowned technology. Using Drowned tech creates a signal it responds to, and it will migrate toward the source. This clears the reactor path — but advances the Drowned activation arc. Players must choose between two converging late-game threats.

attributes.text: **Removal options:**

attributes.text: - **Draw away with Drowned tech** (fast, costs Drowned activation progress)

attributes.text: - **Drive off with force** (requires combined Engineering and Exploration expedition, significant resource cost, does not kill it — it returns in two turns)

attributes.text: Depth Markers are physical dividers inserted into the shuffled draw pile at setup. attributes.text: When players first discover an alien structure (a sub-location card with the `Alien Structure` keyword at Tier 3 or deeper), they report to a GM. entities.name: > *The ocean does not announce itself. It simply becomes more present the deeper you go, until presence is all there is.

entities.name: How to use this document

attributes.text: How to use this document

entities.name: This is not a lore document. It is a writing tool.

attributes.text: This is not a lore document. It is a writing tool.

entities.name: Before writing any card text, read-aloud line, or event description set at a specific tier, check the relevant section h

attributes.text: Before writing any card text, read-aloud line, or event description set at a specific tier, check the relevant section here. The goal is not uniformity — cards should have distinct voices — but coherence. A player who has been reading Tier 1 cards for two hours should feel the difference when they draw their first Tier 3 card, without anyone explaining that the world has changed.

entities.name: Every tier has four registers: **light**, **sound**, **body** (pressure, temperature, physical sensation), and **biology

attributes.text: Every tier has four registers: **light**, **sound**, **body** (pressure, temperature, physical sensation), and **biology** (what the living things are doing). Write to at least two of these per card that describes a place. The deeper the tier, the more the registers should feel like they are coming from the same source.

entities.name: The Depth has a sensory signature that runs from Tier 3 to Tier 5. It builds. By the time players reach Tier 5, it shoul

attributes.text: The Depth has a sensory signature that runs from Tier 3 to Tier 5. It builds. By the time players reach Tier 5, it should feel like something they have been noticing for a long time — not a reveal, but a recognition.

attributes.text: Tier 1   The Sunlit Shallows

entities.name: The experience

attributes.text: The experience

entities.name: Tier 1 is the most legible part of this world. It is genuinely beautiful in a way that is almost disarming — players arr

attributes.text: Tier 1 is the most legible part of this world. It is genuinely beautiful in a way that is almost disarming — players arriving here after the crash should feel the world extending an unearned welcome, which makes what comes later more pointed.

entities.name: The light here is warm and abundant, filtering through shallow water in shifting columns. It moves constantly. The visua

attributes.text: The light here is warm and abundant, filtering through shallow water in shifting columns. It moves constantly. The visual effect is less like being underwater and more like being inside light itself — everything touched by it, nothing quite still.

entities.name: Light

attributes.text: Light

entities.name: Amber-gold in the upper shallows, cooling to pale green at the shelf edge. Visibility is high — thirty metres on a clear

attributes.text: Amber-gold in the upper shallows, cooling to pale green at the shelf edge. Visibility is high — thirty metres on a clear turn, less when the tidal currents stir the organic matter. Shadows are soft and multiple; the light refracts around organisms and formations, creating duplicates. Things look slightly doubled at the edges.

entities.name: At night, or in the shadow of the wreck: the bioluminescence here is incidental, decorative almost — individual organism

attributes.text: At night, or in the shadow of the wreck: the bioluminescence here is incidental, decorative almost — individual organisms pulsing at their own rhythms, uncoordinated, like a city seen from above.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 1 light is generous. It shows you things. Use it to make the world feel accessible.*

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 1 light is generous. It shows you things. Use it to make the world feel accessible.*

entities.name: Sound

attributes.text: Sound

entities.name: Busy. The Tier 1 acoustic environment is the richest in the game — clicks, pulses, the low percussion of shells and form

attributes.text: Busy. The Tier 1 acoustic environment is the richest in the game — clicks, pulses, the low percussion of shells and formations settling, the higher frequencies of small fauna in motion. It reads as noise before it reads as signal.

entities.name: Underneath all of it, at the very bottom of the audible range, there is a tone. It has always been there. Nobody notices

attributes.text: Underneath all of it, at the very bottom of the audible range, there is a tone. It has always been there. Nobody notices it at Tier 1 because there is too much else to hear.

entities.name: *Writing signal: mention the noise. The tone beneath it is not yet worth naming.*

attributes.text: *Writing signal: mention the noise. The tone beneath it is not yet worth naming.*

entities.name: Body

attributes.text: Body

entities.name: Warm. The water at Tier 1 is the closest this ocean gets to comfortable — not tropical, but manageable without full ther

attributes.text: Warm. The water at Tier 1 is the closest this ocean gets to comfortable — not tropical, but manageable without full thermal protection. Current is present but gentle, mostly tidal, predictable. The pressure is almost nothing.

entities.name: Physical effort here is metabolic, not mechanical. The body works to stay warm and oxygenated; the equipment works to fi

attributes.text: Physical effort here is metabolic, not mechanical. The body works to stay warm and oxygenated; the equipment works to filter and recycle. The main physical experience is the weight of the water itself — not hostile, just constant, a reminder that this is not air.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 1 physical discomfort is mild and familiar. Save the body's attention for deeper tiers.*
