attributes.text: Biology

entities.name: Everything is moving. The ecology at Tier 1 is dense and active — grazing fauna on the reef formations, filter feeders i

attributes.text: Everything is moving. The ecology at Tier 1 is dense and active — grazing fauna on the reef formations, filter feeders in the current, small predators cycling through the Flora in patterns that look, with enough observation, almost choreographed.

entities.name: The organisms here are not obviously alien. They have analogues — things that swim like fish, things that wave like anem

attributes.text: The organisms here are not obviously alien. They have analogues — things that swim like fish, things that wave like anemones, things that cluster like coral. The alienness is in the details: the wrong number of appendages, the symmetry that isn't quite bilateral, the colours that don't match any prey-warning or camouflage logic you were taught. You notice it, and then you stop noticing it, which is its own kind of strangeness.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 1 biology is abundant and almost-familiar. The alienness is quiet, detail-level. It should not be

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 1 biology is abundant and almost-familiar. The alienness is quiet, detail-level. It should not be the first thing mentioned.*

entities.name: Tier 2   The Kelp and Ruins

attributes.text: Tier 2   The Kelp and Ruins

entities.name: The experience

attributes.text: The experience

entities.name: Tier 2 is where the world gets its scale. The kelp forests here are not background — they are architecture, vertical and

attributes.text: Tier 2 is where the world gets its scale. The kelp forests here are not background — they are architecture, vertical and massive, creating corridors and chambers and depths-within-depths. Players stop moving across the world and start moving through it.

entities.name: The ruins appear here for the first time. They are almost the right shape. That is what is wrong with them.

attributes.text: The ruins appear here for the first time. They are almost the right shape. That is what is wrong with them.

entities.name: Light

attributes.text: Light

entities.name: The warm amber of the shallows is gone. Light at Tier 2 is filtered through the kelp canopy — green-blue, directional, a

attributes.text: The warm amber of the shallows is gone. Light at Tier 2 is filtered through the kelp canopy — green-blue, directional, arriving in shafts rather than columns. It illuminates vertically, which means the floors of kelp corridors are dim and the mid-water is bright and the canopy is the brightest thing in the world. Movement in the canopy creates moving light on everything below it.

entities.name: In the ruins and the Broken Trenchline: the light is blocked. Pools of near-darkness in structures that were clearly des

attributes.text: In the ruins and the Broken Trenchline: the light is blocked. Pools of near-darkness in structures that were clearly designed for senses that did not depend on it.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 2 light is conditional. It reveals some things and not others, and the player does not always cont

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 2 light is conditional. It reveals some things and not others, and the player does not always control which.*

entities.name: Sound

attributes.text: Sound

entities.name: Quieter than Tier 1, but more structured. The biological noise drops off as the ecosystem changes composition. What rema

attributes.text: Quieter than Tier 1, but more structured. The biological noise drops off as the ecosystem changes composition. What remains: the low creak of kelp in current, the percussion of formations, the occasional distant impact from something large moving in the mid-water.

entities.name: And the tone. Still at the bottom of the range, but louder here — or rather, more audible, because the noise above it ha

attributes.text: And the tone. Still at the bottom of the range, but louder here — or rather, more audible, because the noise above it has thinned. It is not a natural sound. Instruments reading it for the first time will flag it as signal rather than ambient. It does not match any known frequency band. It has been here a long time.

entities.name: *Writing signal: name the tone at Tier 2. Not as a revelation — as a data point. Something to log and move past. Players

attributes.text: *Writing signal: name the tone at Tier 2. Not as a revelation — as a data point. Something to log and move past. Players who pay attention will return to it.*

entities.name: Body

attributes.text: Body

entities.name: Colder. The thermocline between Tier 1 and Tier 2 is the first physical threshold — a drop of several degrees that the b

attributes.text: Colder. The thermocline between Tier 1 and Tier 2 is the first physical threshold — a drop of several degrees that the body registers before the instruments confirm it. Thermal protection becomes necessary rather than optional.

entities.name: Current is more complex here: the tidal patterns that governed Tier 1 interact with the kelp's own resistance, creating

attributes.text: Current is more complex here: the tidal patterns that governed Tier 1 interact with the kelp's own resistance, creating local eddies and backflows. Navigation by feel becomes unreliable. Equipment handles it; the body just notes that the water is less predictable than it was.

entities.name: The ruins, when you enter them: stale. The water inside has been separated from the main circulation long enough to deve

attributes.text: The ruins, when you enter them: stale. The water inside has been separated from the main circulation long enough to develop its own chemistry. Not dangerous, not yet, but different in a way that the body registers as wrong.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 2 introduces cold and complexity. The body is working harder without being in danger yet.*

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 2 introduces cold and complexity. The body is working harder without being in danger yet.*

entities.name: Biology

attributes.text: Biology

entities.name: Less abundant than Tier 1, more specialised. The organisms here have adapted to the vertical environment — flatter profi

attributes.text: Less abundant than Tier 1, more specialised. The organisms here have adapted to the vertical environment — flatter profiles, better low-light sensitivity, different feeding strategies. Predators at Tier 2 are more visible because they move between the lit mid-water and the dark floor, crossing the light rather than hiding from it.

entities.name: The kelp itself. This is not a plant in any sense you were trained for. It does not have roots in the conventional sense

attributes.text: The kelp itself. This is not a plant in any sense you were trained for. It does not have roots in the conventional sense; it anchors to the mineral formations below and feeds on the current above. Its growth patterns are fractal and, at sufficient scale, create structures that look like they were planned. Corridors that run straight for thirty metres before turning at exactly the same angle. Chambers where multiple kelp organisms have grown together into something that functions like a ceiling. You remind yourself it is not deliberate.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 2 biology is adapted and efficient. The organisms are more purposeful-looking. The kelp specifical

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 2 biology is adapted and efficient. The organisms are more purposeful-looking. The kelp specifically should feel like it is making decisions it isn't making.*

entities.name: The ruins   Tier 2 first appearance

attributes.text: The ruins   Tier 2 first appearance

entities.name: The Drowned structures at Tier 2 are partial — grown over, partially collapsed, integrated into the kelp ecosystem in wa

attributes.text: The Drowned structures at Tier 2 are partial — grown over, partially collapsed, integrated into the kelp ecosystem in ways that make them difficult to distinguish from natural formations at a distance.

entities.name: The tell is scale and angle. Natural formations at this depth have the geometry of accumulation — irregular, weighted to

attributes.text: The tell is scale and angle. Natural formations at this depth have the geometry of accumulation — irregular, weighted toward the base, following the path of least resistance. Drowned structures have the geometry of intention: corridors that continue past the point where a natural passage would have closed, chambers with walls that meet at angles geology does not produce, openings at heights that imply the body that used them was a specific size.

entities.name: Up close, the material is wrong. Not wrong like an alien mineral — wrong like something that was grown according to a pl

attributes.text: Up close, the material is wrong. Not wrong like an alien mineral — wrong like something that was grown according to a plan. The substrate is biological but structured, layered in a way that organic growth does not produce unassisted. It is the difference between a coral formation and a coral formation that someone helped.

entities.name: No inscriptions here. No records. Just structure, and the fact of it.

attributes.text: No inscriptions here. No records. Just structure, and the fact of it.

entities.name: *Writing signal: first contact with the ruins is sensory, not informational. They are wrong in a way that takes a moment

attributes.text: *Writing signal: first contact with the ruins is sensory, not informational. They are wrong in a way that takes a moment to name. Do not explain what they are. Describe what is strange about them.*

entities.name: Tier 3   The Twilight Shelf

attributes.text: Tier 3   The Twilight Shelf

entities.name: The experience

attributes.text: The experience

entities.name: Tier 3 is where the world stops being almost-familiar. The shift is not dramatic — there is no single moment — but by th

attributes.text: Tier 3 is where the world stops being almost-familiar. The shift is not dramatic — there is no single moment — but by the time a player has read several Tier 3 cards, they should feel that they are somewhere genuinely different. The biology is stranger. The light is doing something the light in Tiers 1 and 2 was not doing. The Depth is present for the first time in a way that can be felt rather than measured.

entities.name: Light

attributes.text: Light

entities.name: Solar light is gone. What remains is entirely biological — the bioluminescence of the organisms at this depth, which is

attributes.text: Solar light is gone. What remains is entirely biological — the bioluminescence of the organisms at this depth, which is not incidental or decorative but structural. The organisms here produce light as a primary sense: navigation, communication, predation, display. The result is an environment that is lit from within and from many directions simultaneously, with no single source.

entities.name: The bioluminescence at Tier 3 is blue-green in dominant frequency, with pulses of violet and, rarely, amber. Individual

attributes.text: The bioluminescence at Tier 3 is blue-green in dominant frequency, with pulses of violet and, rarely, amber. Individual organisms have their own frequencies. Schools of fauna produce interference patterns when they move together — bands of light and dark that travel through the water like a visible sound.

entities.name: And the patterns are not random. Not obviously coordinated, not consciously produced — but not random. A biologist payin

attributes.text: And the patterns are not random. Not obviously coordinated, not consciously produced — but not random. A biologist paying attention will notice, sometime in the second or third expedition to a Tier 3 location, that the light pulses are not independent. Something is influencing the phase. Whatever it is, it is operating below the threshold of any individual organism's awareness.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 3 light is alive and patterned. It comes from the biology, not from above. Use it to light scenes

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 3 light is alive and patterned. It comes from the biology, not from above. Use it to light scenes from below and from the sides, never from above. The patterns should be noticeable without being explicable.*

entities.name: Sound

attributes.text: Sound

entities.name: The biological noise has dropped further. Tier 3 is acoustically spare — the fauna here are larger, slower, more widely

attributes.text: The biological noise has dropped further. Tier 3 is acoustically spare — the fauna here are larger, slower, more widely spaced. What sound there is carries further than it should.

entities.name: The tone is louder. It is no longer a data point to be logged and set aside. It sits at the lower edge of what the body

attributes.text: The tone is louder. It is no longer a data point to be logged and set aside. It sits at the lower edge of what the body can feel as vibration rather than hear as sound — a pressure in the chest, a resonance in the bones of the hands that are holding the instruments. Instruments confirm it as signal. The frequency is consistent. It does not drift or pulse. It has been broadcasting, at the same frequency, for longer than anyone's instruments can date.

entities.name: At Tier 3, for the first time, the tone seems to change when something significant happens nearby — when an ecosystem is

attributes.text: At Tier 3, for the first time, the tone seems to change when something significant happens nearby — when an ecosystem is damaged, when a Drowned structure is activated, when a large organism dies. Not dramatically. A half-step shift that lasts for approximately one turn and then returns to baseline. It is the first indication that the tone is responsive rather than passive.

entities.name: *Writing signal: the tone becomes physical at Tier 3. Write it as something felt before it is heard. The responsiveness

attributes.text: *Writing signal: the tone becomes physical at Tier 3. Write it as something felt before it is heard. The responsiveness should be noted by instruments first; players who feel it without instruments have noticed something important.*

entities.name: Body

attributes.text: Body

entities.name: Cold and pressured. Thermal protection is essential; the equipment is working continuously. Pressure at Tier 3 is the fi

attributes.text: Cold and pressured. Thermal protection is essential; the equipment is working continuously. Pressure at Tier 3 is the first that requires mechanical assistance — without the right rating, the body begins to report problems. Nothing immediately dangerous at the top of the tier, but present and accumulating.

entities.name: The current here is the first place the breath-current can be felt.

attributes.text: The current here is the first place the breath-current can be felt.

entities.name: The breath-current is not a tidal or thermal phenomenon. It is too slow, too regular, and its source is not identifiable

attributes.text: The breath-current is not a tidal or thermal phenomenon. It is too slow, too regular, and its source is not identifiable by any instrument. It moves against the local hydrological flow — not violently, a gentle consistent pressure that comes from below and slightly to one side, as if the water is being exhaled by something very large and very patient. It is strongest in the Lantern Drop's fissures and in the still basins of the Echo Basins. It is absent in the Drift Graveyard.

entities.name: Players who notice it tend to describe it the same way, without coordination: it feels like being close to something tha

attributes.text: Players who notice it tend to describe it the same way, without coordination: it feels like being close to something that is breathing.

entities.name: *Writing signal: introduce the breath-current at Tier 3 as a physical detail, not a dramatic revelation. The players who

attributes.text: *Writing signal: introduce the breath-current at Tier 3 as a physical detail, not a dramatic revelation. The players who notice it may not report it. The players who report it may not be believed. Both responses are correct.*

entities.name: Biology

attributes.text: Biology

entities.name: Stranger. The organisms at Tier 3 are not analogues for anything; the framework of almost-familiar is gone. Filter feede

attributes.text: Stranger. The organisms at Tier 3 are not analogues for anything; the framework of almost-familiar is gone. Filter feeders the size of a small vehicle, anchored to fissures in the shelf wall, trailing structures that look like antennae and may be. Predators that navigate by the bioluminescence of their prey rather than by sight — their own light suppressed, moving through the patterns they are hunting.

entities.name: The Void Drifters are the organism that most directly expresses the Tier 3 uncanny. They are neutrally buoyant, very slo

attributes.text: The Void Drifters are the organism that most directly expresses the Tier 3 uncanny. They are neutrally buoyant, very slow, and appear to have no active propulsion. They move with the breath-current. Whether they are following it or producing it is not determinable from observation. They are beautiful and uncomfortable to look at for extended periods, in a way that players should feel but not be able to explain.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 3 biology should read as purposeful in ways the organisms cannot intend. Avoid describing organism

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 3 biology should read as purposeful in ways the organisms cannot intend. Avoid describing organisms as intelligent or aware — describe them as behaving as if the environment itself were guiding them.*

entities.name: The ruins   Tier 3

attributes.text: The ruins   Tier 3

entities.name: The Drowned structures at Tier 3 are intact and deliberately placed. Not grown over — maintained, in the sense that the

attributes.text: The Drowned structures at Tier 3 are intact and deliberately placed. Not grown over — maintained, in the sense that the biological substrate they are built from continues to be alive and active. The structures are tending themselves.

entities.name: The inscriptions begin here. Not the dense records of Tier 4 — single glyphs, repeated at thresholds, at doorways, at th

attributes.text: The inscriptions begin here. Not the dense records of Tier 4 — single glyphs, repeated at thresholds, at doorways, at the edges of what seem to be designated spaces. They appear to be warnings, or markers, or both. Players cannot read them. The feeling they produce — careful, specific, the impression that someone very deliberate put them there — is more useful than any translation.

entities.name: The structures at Tier 3 are larger than at Tier 2, and their geometry is more obviously wrong. The repeating angles fro

attributes.text: The structures at Tier 3 are larger than at Tier 2, and their geometry is more obviously wrong. The repeating angles from Tier 2 are here at a scale that makes them impossible to rationalise as accident. A chamber 40 metres across with a ceiling that meets the floor at exactly the same angle on all sides. A corridor that slopes downward at a gradient too precise to be natural, leading to a door that is sealed in a way that has not degraded in however long it has been closed.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 3 ruins feel inhabited even though they are empty. The maintenance-without-maintainer detail is im

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 3 ruins feel inhabited even though they are empty. The maintenance-without-maintainer detail is important. Write them as places that are still in use, by something.*

entities.name: Tier 4   The Blackwater Depths

attributes.text: Tier 4   The Blackwater Depths

entities.name: The experience

attributes.text: The experience

entities.name: Tier 4 is the dark. Not metaphorically — the solar spectrum is completely absent, and the bioluminescence that lit Tier

attributes.text: Tier 4 is the dark. Not metaphorically — the solar spectrum is completely absent, and the bioluminescence that lit Tier 3 is sparser here, distributed differently, produced by organisms whose light-use is less communicative and more defensive. The dominant visual experience is objects emerging from blackness and returning to it.

entities.name: This is also where the Drowned become legible as people. The emotional register of Tier 4 should feel like the sensory r

attributes.text: This is also where the Drowned become legible as people. The emotional register of Tier 4 should feel like the sensory register: things emerging from the dark that are recognisable, at close range, as having once been alive and arguing and afraid.

entities.name: Light

attributes.text: Light

entities.name: Bioluminescence at Tier 4 is cold and blue-white, high contrast against total darkness. Individual organisms produce it

attributes.text: Bioluminescence at Tier 4 is cold and blue-white, high contrast against total darkness. Individual organisms produce it in bursts — a brief illumination, then dark again. The effect is stroboscopic when fauna are active, static when they are not.

entities.name: The ruins glow. This is the first significant distinction from Tier 3: Drowned structures at Tier 4 produce their own li

attributes.text: The ruins glow. This is the first significant distinction from Tier 3: Drowned structures at Tier 4 produce their own light, from the biological substrate they are built from, and that light is a different frequency from any organism at this depth. It is the wrong blue — slightly too green, slightly too regular, pulsing on the tone's frequency rather than on any biological rhythm. Players who have been tracking the tone will notice this. The ruins are responsive to it.

entities.name: At the record rooms specifically: the inscribed walls produce faint light along the inscription channels. The density of

attributes.text: At the record rooms specifically: the inscribed walls produce faint light along the inscription channels. The density of inscription means some walls glow nearly continuously. Walking through a record room at Tier 4 is walking through a space lit by what the people who built it wrote on the walls.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 4 light is cold, high contrast, and comes from the wrong places. The ruins' glow should feel like

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 4 light is cold, high contrast, and comes from the wrong places. The ruins' glow should feel like a distinction before it is understood as one.*

entities.name: Sound

attributes.text: Sound

entities.name: The tone is the dominant acoustic feature at Tier 4. The biological noise has nearly gone — the fauna here are large, sl

attributes.text: The tone is the dominant acoustic feature at Tier 4. The biological noise has nearly gone — the fauna here are large, slow, and widely spaced; their acoustic signatures are low-frequency and intermittent. What remains between those signatures is the tone.

entities.name: At Tier 4, the tone is loud enough to hear without instruments in a quiet moment, though most players will hear it as a

attributes.text: At Tier 4, the tone is loud enough to hear without instruments in a quiet moment, though most players will hear it as a low pressure in the ears rather than a sound. Sensitive instruments can now resolve it into a complex signal — not a single frequency but a chord, multiple harmonics in a relationship that is stable and very old. It does not change in response to events here the way it did at Tier 3. At Tier 4, it is continuous and unvarying, which is its own kind of strangeness.

entities.name: The record rooms have their own acoustic property: the chamber geometries seem designed to amplify the tone. Whether the

attributes.text: The record rooms have their own acoustic property: the chamber geometries seem designed to amplify the tone. Whether the Drowned built them this way deliberately, or whether the rooms have settled into resonance with it over time, is not determinable.

entities.name: *Writing signal: the tone is now a presence. At Tier 4 it should be mentioned before the visual description in any read-

attributes.text: *Writing signal: the tone is now a presence. At Tier 4 it should be mentioned before the visual description in any read-aloud text. It arrives first.*

entities.name: Body

attributes.text: Body

entities.name: Cold. Tier 4 cold is not the sharp cold of Tier 3 — it is deep and consistent, a cold that the equipment manages but can

attributes.text: Cold. Tier 4 cold is not the sharp cold of Tier 3 — it is deep and consistent, a cold that the equipment manages but cannot fully offset. Prolonged stays at Tier 4 produce metabolic cost even with full thermal protection; expeditions are time-limited by biology as much as by oxygen.

entities.name: The pressure at Tier 4 is significant. Without correct equipment it is immediately dangerous. With correct equipment it

attributes.text: The pressure at Tier 4 is significant. Without correct equipment it is immediately dangerous. With correct equipment it is a continuous weight — not painful, but present in every movement, every breath. Players should feel it as attention required to manage.

entities.name: The breath-current is present at Tier 4 but changed. At Tier 3 it was a gentle consistent pressure from below. At Tier 4

attributes.text: The breath-current is present at Tier 4 but changed. At Tier 3 it was a gentle consistent pressure from below. At Tier 4 it is intermittent — absent for long periods, then present for a turn or two, stronger than before. The pattern of its absence and presence does not match any tidal or thermal schedule. Some expeditions feel it constantly; some feel it not at all. There is no instrument that correlates the variation with any other measurable condition.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 4 cold and pressure are a background cost. Write them as labour — the effort of being somewhere di

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 4 cold and pressure are a background cost. Write them as labour — the effort of being somewhere difficult. The breath-current's intermittency at Tier 4 is more unsettling than its consistency at Tier 3.*

entities.name: Biology

attributes.text: Biology

entities.name: Sparse, large, strange. The organisms at Tier 4 are apex-level — nothing here is prey for anything shallower. Their biol

attributes.text: Sparse, large, strange. The organisms at Tier 4 are apex-level — nothing here is prey for anything shallower. Their bioluminescence is defensive or predatory rather than communicative; they do not flock or school. They move through the dark in ones and twos.

entities.name: The Bone Fields' eponymous feature: the skeletal remains of organisms that have no living analogue at any shallower dept

attributes.text: The Bone Fields' eponymous feature: the skeletal remains of organisms that have no living analogue at any shallower depth. Whatever produced these remains is either extinct or present only at Tier 5. The bones themselves are a biological material that has partially mineralised over geological time — they are as much stone as bone, and they are vast. Players walking through the Bone Fields are walking through the ribs of something that makes the Depth Stalker look small.

entities.name: The ecology here is at the edge of what can be sustained without extraordinary inputs. The Drowned maintained it through

attributes.text: The ecology here is at the edge of what can be sustained without extraordinary inputs. The Drowned maintained it through their systems. Without that maintenance, Tier 4 ecosystems are in slow decline — present, functional, but thinning. Players who understand what they are looking at will recognise this as a consequence of the Drowned's disappearance, not a natural state.

entities.name: *Writing signal: Tier 4 biology should feel like aftermath. The scale of the bones establishes what was here. The curren

attributes.text: *Writing signal: Tier 4 biology should feel like aftermath. The scale of the bones establishes what was here. The current sparseness establishes what is gone.*

entities.name: Tier 5   The Abyssal Core

attributes.text: Tier 5   The Abyssal Core

entities.name: *Two locations. Two registers. The world's two oldest things.*

attributes.text: *Two locations. Two registers. The world's two oldest things.*

entities.name: The Reactor Site   Fire

attributes.text: The Reactor Site   Fire

entities.name: *The location toward which Restorationists move. The Sinkhole Gate leads here.*

attributes.text: *The location toward which Restorationists move. The Sinkhole Gate leads here.*

entities.name: This is not a natural thermal site. The reactor's descent and the Drowned's deep infrastructure have interacted in ways

attributes.text: This is not a natural thermal site. The reactor's descent and the Drowned's deep infrastructure have interacted in ways that Engineering cannot fully model. The result is a site that is geothermally active in patterns that do not match the local geology — irregular, intense, producing heat plumes that make the water visible as distortion.

entities.name: **Light:** orange and red. The only warm light in the deep ocean, and it is the light of something broken. Bioluminescen

attributes.text: **Light:** orange and red. The only warm light in the deep ocean, and it is the light of something broken. Bioluminescence here is suppressed or absent — the organisms that survived the reactor's arrival are adapted to unusual radiation and chemistry, not to low light. Some of them glow in frequencies that are not bioluminescence in any biological sense; instruments flag these as reactor fluorescence.

entities.name: The ruins near the reactor site are damaged — not by the crash directly, but by the thermal and chemical changes that fo

attributes.text: The ruins near the reactor site are damaged — not by the crash directly, but by the thermal and chemical changes that followed it. The biological substrate is partially dead. Walls that glowed at other Tier 4 and 5 sites are dark here. The tone is present but distorted — the reactor's own emissions create interference that breaks the chord into fragments.

entities.name: **Body:** hot. The first time in the ocean that the threat is heat rather than cold. Thermal protection works in reverse

attributes.text: **Body:** hot. The first time in the ocean that the threat is heat rather than cold. Thermal protection works in reverse here; the equipment adapted for Tier 4 cold is badly suited to Tier 5 heat, and players who have not prepared will feel it immediately.

entities.name: The reactor site is the one place in the deep ocean where the Depth seems absent. The breath-current does not reach here

attributes.text: The reactor site is the one place in the deep ocean where the Depth seems absent. The breath-current does not reach here. The tone is broken. Whatever the Depth is, it has withdrawn from this specific location — not abandoned it, but unable to be fully present within the reactor's disruption field.

entities.name: *Writing signal: the reactor site should feel like an intrusion. Everything that makes the deep ocean feel like it has i

attributes.text: *Writing signal: the reactor site should feel like an intrusion. Everything that makes the deep ocean feel like it has its own logic and presence is muted or absent here. It is the humans' mess, in the Depth's world.*

entities.name: The Cage Site   Ice

attributes.text: The Cage Site   Ice

entities.name: *The location toward which Transcendence and Preservationist players move. The Cold Eye.*

attributes.text: *The location toward which Transcendence and Preservationist players move. The Cold Eye.*

entities.name: The coldest place in the ocean. The cage's operation produces a thermal sink — drawing heat from the surrounding water a

attributes.text: The coldest place in the ocean. The cage's operation produces a thermal sink — drawing heat from the surrounding water as a component of its regulatory function. The Cold Eye is named for what instruments show when they are pointed at its centre: a temperature reading that should not be possible at this depth, in this ocean, on any world where thermodynamics applies normally.

entities.name: **Light:** none. The Cold Eye produces no light. The organisms here — few, ancient, extremely slow — produce no biolumin

attributes.text: **Light:** none. The Cold Eye produces no light. The organisms here — few, ancient, extremely slow — produce no bioluminescence. The ruins produce no glow. There is total darkness at the Cold Eye, and the darkness is deliberate.

entities.name: Players who arrive here without significant light sources see nothing. Players who arrive with light sources see the cag

attributes.text: Players who arrive here without significant light sources see nothing. Players who arrive with light sources see the cage.

entities.name: The cage does not look like engineering. It does not look biological. It looks like both of those things simultaneously,

attributes.text: The cage does not look like engineering. It does not look biological. It looks like both of those things simultaneously, and like neither — a structure that has been here long enough to become part of the geology, that uses the pressure and temperature gradients of the deep ocean as load-bearing elements, that is alive in the way a very old tree is alive — mostly mineral, still growing at the edges, the life in it more structure than process.

entities.name: It is very large. Larger than the ship. Larger than anything the players have built.

attributes.text: It is very large. Larger than the ship. Larger than anything the players have built.

entities.name: **Sound:** the tone is loudest here. At the Cold Eye, it is not a tone any longer — it is the full chord, resolved, pres

attributes.text: **Sound:** the tone is loudest here. At the Cold Eye, it is not a tone any longer — it is the full chord, resolved, present as something the body receives rather than the ears hear. Players who have the Alien Attunement icon experience it differently from those who do not. For those who do: it is the closest thing to communication the Depth attempts in the game. Not language. Not instruction. Orientation — the feeling of being shown where you are in relation to everything else.

entities.name: **Body:** cold beyond cold. The equipment manages it. The body manages it. But prolonged presence at the Cold Eye produc

attributes.text: **Body:** cold beyond cold. The equipment manages it. The body manages it. But prolonged presence at the Cold Eye produces something that is not physiological — a stillness, a slowing of thought, an attention that is not quite voluntary. Players sometimes describe Tier 5 expeditions to the Cold Eye as feeling longer than the clock says they were.

entities.name: The breath-current: constant here. Stronger than anywhere above. At the Cold Eye, it is not ambiguous — it is clearly a

attributes.text: The breath-current: constant here. Stronger than anywhere above. At the Cold Eye, it is not ambiguous — it is clearly a respiration, clearly regular, clearly coming from something that is very large and very present and has been here for a very long time.

entities.name: *Writing signal: the Cold Eye should feel like arrival. Everything in the sensory vocabulary that has been building sinc

attributes.text: *Writing signal: the Cold Eye should feel like arrival. Everything in the sensory vocabulary that has been building since Tier 3 — the tone, the breath-current, the Depth's presence — reaches its fullest expression here. Not a revelation, but a recognition. Players who have been paying attention will feel that they have been moving toward this place since the first time they noticed something they couldn't explain.*

attributes.text: **Card 5 and "What the Bones Know":** The existing Bone Fields final card reads aloud: *"They did not die. They were moved…"* — this is the Listeners' story, told at one remove. Card 5 (Final Transmission) tells the same story directly, from inside. The two cards should be felt as the same revelation arriving twice: once as archaeological inference, once as a voice.

entities.name: **Warning Token note:** Cards 3 and 4 interact with Warning Tokens asymmetrically — Card 3 adds one; Card 4 removes none

attributes.text: **Warning Token note:** Cards 3 and 4 interact with Warning Tokens asymmetrically — Card 3 adds one; Card 4 removes none and notes the silence instead. This is intentional. The Harvester story does not clean up after itself.

entities.name: **Philosophy reveals:** Cards 1 and 2 include Control notes about player reactions. These are the richest philosophy-sur

attributes.text: **Philosophy reveals:** Cards 1 and 2 include Control notes about player reactions. These are the richest philosophy-surfacing moments in the Tier 4 arc. Facilitate them deliberately — slow the pace, let the read-aloud land, watch the table.

entities.name: A Rough Landing

fields.Name: A Rough Landing
fields.Back Text:
Read aloud and follow instructions on the backs of cards (like this one) as they are revealed. They will walk you through playing the game.

This deck will introduce you to the Ecology Department on the A.E.V. Aphelion, and the Reef Garden location.

Draw this card now and read the other side.
fields.Front Text:
You enter your cryo-pod filled with hope, to be selection for a survey mission on board the E.S.S. Aphelion is a rare honour, the finest research starship takes onto the finest crew.
You drift into your induced slumber, dreaming of the discoveries you will be part of…
You wake from your cryo-pod with a start - sirens blazing, metal buckling, sparks flying.
There is just enough time to reach an escape pod, you watch from its window as the Aphelion splits in two and rains debris down on the water world you had come to study.
You find yourself bobbing on the sea, sharing your pod with the other survivors from your department, surrounded by the wreckage of the Aphelion.
fields.Designer Notes: Mirrors PDF page 2, retargeted to Ecology.

entities.name: Ecology Department

fields.Name: Ecology Department
fields.Back Text:
You are a member of the Ecology Department.

Reveal the next cards (3-4). Each player chooses 1 to keep and reads its back side privately.
fields.Front Text:
The Ecology Department is responsible for understanding and tending the living systems of this world.

Goals:
1) Understand the flora and fauna of this world.
2) Work out how to generate a reliable source of food and water.
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror card 2. Only 2 of 5 Ecology roles in this playtest.

entities.name: Lead Ecologist

fields.Name: Lead Ecologist
fields.Back Text:
Head of the Ecology field team. Coordinates surveys, prevents cascading losses.

Passive: Diver
[1 Oxygen Icon]

Icons, like the Oxygen icon above, are used as prerequisites for actions and expeditions. They are not consumed.
fields.Front Text:
DO NOT SHOW THIS SIDE TO OTHER PLAYERS.

This planet is not just a resource. The reef systems here, the kelp forests, the deep-water biology – they are extraordinary. Exploitation will destroy them. You want the group to survive, but not at any price.

Personal Goals:
1) Stop anyone from despoiling the planet.
2) If the group leaves, ensure the planet is left in a condition close to how you found it.
fields.Designer Notes: From existing xlsx EC-1.

entities.name: Systems Ecologist

fields.Name: Systems Ecologist
fields.Back Text:
You grow things. That's not a simple skill here – the "soil" is a mineral analogue, the light is wrong, and the organisms you're working with are alien – but the principles hold. Water, nutrients, growth cycles, yield.

Passive: Cultivator
Increase the Population Track of one Flora card at your location by 1.

Location cards often have tracks that track the health or resources of that card. They can be raised and lowered but never beyond the ends of the track.
fields.Front Text:
DO NOT SHOW THIS SIDE TO OTHER PLAYERS.

This world is a paradise and a chance for a fresh start.  You don’t want to escape, you want a colony that works in the long-term.

Personal Goals:
1) Demonstrate that a permanent colony here could be nutritionally self-sufficient.
fields.Designer Notes: From existing xlsx EC-2.

entities.name: Phase Reference

fields.Name: Phase Reference
fields.Back Text:
Each turn there will be a 15 minute Exploration phase.
You can form a team from any players you wish to visit one location, following the instructions on the deck there.
Any remaining time can be spent talking to any player who isn’t on an expedition.

Set this card aside and play the Exploration Phase now with the rest of your department.
Once the Exploration phase is over flip this card to see the Upkeep phase rules.
fields.Front Text:
After the Exploration phase is a 5 minute Upkeep phase.
All players must choose an outpost to stay in and resolve the upkeep rules of all cards in hand and at their location, in an order of their choosing.
Players must remain at their location for the duration of the upkeep phase.

Once the Upkeep phase is over flip this card to see the Exploration phase rules.
fields.Designer Notes: Identical to Crash Flats card 8.

entities.name: Reef Garden Outpost

fields.Name: Reef Garden Outpost
fields.Back Text:
Looking at your surroundings you find yourselves in a shallow sea. Diving below reveals a coral reef, rich with life. The wreckage of your escape pod will suffice for a makeshift outpost.

For this introductory turn you are exploring Reef Garden together.

Immediately draw this card and set its Rations Track to 5.

A token track is a row of numbers on the card, place a cube on it. A track cannot go beyond its maximum or minimum values.
fields.Front Text:
Upkeep

Hydroponics: Refill the rations track by 1 per Energy icon present.

Rations: Each player here must either have a Food icon, reduce the population track of a flora by 1, or reduce the Rations Track by 1.
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror card 9.

entities.name: Shallowwater Filterweed

fields.Name: Shallowwater Filterweed
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Lazy ribbons of pale green weed clinging to the reef. Filters seawater into oxygen and can be processed into an edible mash.

Icons
Provides 1 Oxygen icon while 3+ Pop.

Upkeep
Pop 0 – No effect
Pop 1 – +1 Pop
Pop 2-4 – +2 Population
Pop 5 – No effect
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror. No hand effect (ecosystem card).

entities.name: Spotted Grazers

fields.Name: Spotted Grazers
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Small shoaling fish that graze the Filterweed and the Coral Shelf algae.

Upkeep
Can spend Population to get Biomass.

Pop 0 – No effect
Pop 1-2 – -1 Population from Fauna then +1 Pop, else -1 Pop
Pop 3-4 – -2 Population from Fauna then +2 Pop, else -2 Pop
Pop 5 – -3 Population from Fauna, else -2 Pop
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror card 11. No hand effect.

entities.name: Coral Shelf Formation

fields.Name: Coral Shelf Formation
fields.Back Text:
Minerals, Coral and other crafting ingredients can be used to craft items, which can be found on the crafting table and must be made at an outpost during the Upkeep phase.
Immediately draw this card and set its abundance track to 4.
fields.Front Text:
A broad shelf of brittle living coral.

Upkeep

Choose one:
(a) convert any amount of Abundance into an equal amount of Materials and/or Coral
(b) +1 Abundance.
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror. Permanent trash on exhaustion. No hand effect.

entities.name: Reef Ecologist's Notes

fields.Name: Reef Ecologist's Notes
fields.Back Text:
Knowledge cards can be gained to a player’s hand during an expedition when certain conditions are met.

Set this card beside the deck with this side up.

Gain this card when two cards here have 4+ population.
fields.Front Text:
Icons
[1 Knowledge Icon]

Upkeep
Take 1 Reef Fauna or Flora card into your hand.

Expedition
Play 1 Reef Fauna or Flora card into your current location.
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror card 13.

entities.name: Spawning Ground

fields.Name: Spawning Ground
fields.Back Text:
Some cards have decisions to make during an expedition. The group must choose an option unanimously.

Spawning Ground

You find a spawning ground for the Spotted Grazers. Choose one of the options below, then flip this card to resolve:
A — Harvest resources to help hydroponics.
B — Protect the site from interference
C — Tag & Monitor the creatures.
fields.Front Text:
Harvest or Tag & Monitor: Tuck this card under the Reef Outpost to leave the corresponding icon visible.

Harvest: [Food Icon]
Tag & Monitor: [Knowledge Icon]

Protect: +2 population to Shallowwater Filterweed and +2 population  to Spotted Grazers.

Outpost cards tuck under an outpost and can only be moved if they have arrows on them.
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror card 14. Control notes who argued which option.

entities.name: Reef Caverns

fields.Name: Reef Caverns
fields.Back Text:
Exploration Phase: You can start an exploration here by flipping an reading this card if you meet the following requirements:

2 [Oxygen] + 2 [Knowledge].

Requirements can be met by cards in hand or at this location.
fields.Front Text:
You descend through a vertical chimney in the reef shelf. Light fades, then re-emerges — bluish, intermittent, breathing. The cavern walls glow with something alive.

Set this card aside with this side up.
fields.Designer Notes: PDF mirror card 15. Gateway to the 7-card Reef Cavern sub-deck.

entities.name: Glow-Polyp Mat

fields.Name: Glow-Polyp Mat
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
A pulsing carpet of bioluminescent polyps lining the cavern walls.

Icons: 
Pop 4+ produces 1 Power token

Upkeep:
If Echoing Calcite Spires Abundance is 2+ then +1 pop
If 2+ Reactor icons, -1 pop
fields.Designer Notes: First cavern Power source. No hand effect.

entities.name: Crystalblind Snapper

fields.Name: Crystalblind Snapper
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Eyeless apex predator that hunts by vibration.

Upkeep:
Pop 1-3 must consume 1 Population of Prey and gain 1 Population, else lose 1 population.
Pop 4-5 must consume 2 Population of Prey and gain 1 Population, else lose 1 population.
fields.Designer Notes: Apex Fauna of the cavern. No hand effect.

entities.name: Echoing Calcite Spires

fields.Name: Echoing Calcite Spires
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its abundance track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Spires of resonant calcite that hum when bioluminescence pulses across them.

Upkeep:
Population 2+ Generates 1 Materials/turn.

If Glow-Polyp Mat population is 4+ then +1 abundance
If 3+ Reactor icons, -1 pop
fields.Designer Notes: Knowledge icon source in the cavern. No hand effect.

entities.name: Drowned Survey Cache

fields.Name: Drowned Survey Cache
fields.Back Text:
Some Knowledge cards have unlock conditions that span multiple cards in play.

Set aside with this side up. Gain when conditions are met.

Gain when Glow-Polyp Mat AND Echoing Calcite Spires are both in play here at 4+.
fields.Front Text:
A sealed survey drum from a previous expedition — not yours.

[1 Knowledge icon]

Trash: Ask Control any one question about a location.
fields.Designer Notes: Mid-late cavern Knowledge. Foreshadows the Drowned arc.

entities.name: The Watcher in the Dark

fields.Name: The Watcher in the Dark
fields.Back Text:
Something large drifts past at the edge of the cavern's light. It does not approach. It does not leave.

Immediately draw this card.
fields.Front Text:
Upkeep

All Fauna here at Pop 3+ loses 1 Pop
If no Population was lost it moves on (hand this card to control).
fields.Designer Notes: Sets up the Aphelion Wraith intrusion.

entities.name: Bioluminescent Pollination

fields.Name: Bioluminescent Pollination
fields.Back Text:
You watch a single polyp release a cloud of bright spores. They drift down — and the calcite spires bloom in answer. Something old is still alive here, and it is generous.

Immediately draw this card into hand.
fields.Front Text:
Upkeep

A Flora card you move gains +1 Pop on arrival if at Depth 3+.
fields.Designer Notes: Final card cannot be trashed per design.md §3.2.

entities.name: A Rough Landing

fields.Name: A Rough Landing
fields.Back Text:
Read aloud and follow instructions on the backs of cards (like this one) as they are revealed. They will walk you through playing the game.

This deck will introduce you to the Engineering Department on the A.E.V. Aphelion, and the Crash Flats location.

Draw this card now and read the other side.

You drift into your induced slumber, dreaming of the discoveries you will be part of…
You wake from your cryo-pod with a start - sirens blazing, metal buckling, sparks flying.

entities.name: Engineering Department

fields.Name: Engineering Department
fields.Back Text:
You are a member of the Engineering Department.

Reveal the next card (3). “Each player” “chooses” 1 to keep and reads its back side privately.
fields.Front Text:
The Engineering Department is responsible for everything that was built and everything that needs to be built: outposts, power, fabrication, vehicle maintenance, the reactor itself.

Goals

1) Get as much technology operational again as possible.
2) Search for any new technology.
fields.Designer Notes: Only Fabrication Lead is in this playtest deck.

entities.name: Fabrication Lead

fields.Name: Fabrication Lead
fields.Back Text:
You turn raw materials into outpost upgrades, expedition equipment, power converters, recycling systems.

Passive: Personal Generator
[Power Icon]
fields.Front Text:
DO NOT SHOW THIS SIDE TO OTHER PLAYERS.

This planet has extraordinary resources, and you are in a dire situation. The smart approach is to extract, build, and get back on your feet as soon as possible.

Personal Goals
1) .

entities.name: Crash Flats Outpost (Fabrication Bay)

fields.Name: Crash Flats Outpost (Fabrication Bay)
fields.Back Text:
You drag a torn section of the Aphelion's outer hull onto the sandbar. With the auxiliary fabricator still working, this will do.

For this introductory turn you are exploring Crash Flats together.

Immediately draw this card and set its Rations Track to 5.

A token track is a row of numbers on the card, place a cube on it. A track cannot go beyond its maximum or minimum values.
fields.Front Text:
Upkeep

Fabricator: All items crafted here require 1 fewer resource (of your choice).

Rations: Each player here must either have a Food icon, reduce the population track of a flora by 1, or reduce the Rations Track by 1.
fields.Designer Notes: Engineering analogue of Reef Garden Outpost.

entities.name: Tidal Rust Bloom

fields.Name: Tidal Rust Bloom
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Iron-loving algal mats that bloom over submerged wreckage, slowly breaking down hull plating into reusable material.

Upkeep
Pop 2+ produces 1 Materials/turn
Pop 4+ also produces 1 Food.

If Abundance 3+ on Wreck keyword cards → +1 Pop/turn
No Wreckage keyword present here → -1 Pop/turn.
fields.Designer Notes: Mirrors Filterweed slot — Engineering-flavoured. No hand effect.

entities.name: Carrier Crabs

fields.Name: Carrier Crabs
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Crustaceans that move shell-pieces and scrap between tide-pools — accidental couriers.

Icons
Pop 3+ and Wreck Abundance 3+ produces 1 Materials/turn

Upkeep
If there are no Wreckage with Abundance 2+, -1 Pop.
Pop 0 – No effect
Pop 1-2 – -1 Population from Fauna then +1 Pop, else -1 Pop
Pop 3-4 – -2 Population from Fauna then +2 Pop, else -2 Pop
Pop 5 – -3 Population from Fauna, else -2 Pop
fields.Designer Notes: Mirrors Spotted Grazers — Materials instead of Biomass. No hand effect.

entities.name: Aphelion Wreckage Field

fields.Name: Aphelion Wreckage Field
fields.Back Text:
Minerals, Coral, and other crafting ingredients can be used to craft items. Items are built from salvage at an outpost during Upkeep.

Immediately draw this card and set its Abundance Track to 5.
fields.Front Text:
Spilled hull, panels, and unprocessed alloy — finite, but rich.

Upkeep: convert any amount of Abundance into twice that amount of Materials
fields.Designer Notes: Mirrors Coral Shelf. Permanent trash on exhaustion. No hand effect.

entities.name: Salvage Manifest

fields.Name: Salvage Manifest
fields.Back Text:
Knowledge cards can be gained to a player’s hand during an expedition when certain conditions are met.

Set this card beside the deck with this side up.

A water-damaged inventory of what the Aphelion was carrying.

Gain when 3 Aphelion Salvage recipes are present at this location.
fields.Front Text:
A water-damaged inventory of what the Aphelion was carrying.

Icons
2 [Knowledge icons] when creating Aphelion Salvage items.
fields.Designer Notes: Mirrors PDF card 13 slot — Engineering-themed.

entities.name: The Power Question

fields.Name: The Power Question
fields.Back Text:
Some cards have decisions to make during an expedition. The group must choose an option unanimously.

You find the auxiliary reactor still warm. The hull around it shows hairline fractures.

A — Restart it.
B — Strip for parts.
C — Seal it away.
fields.Front Text:
A — Restart it: gain 2 Power icons, the Reactor track advances 1 (see control)
B — Strip for parts: Trash this card to restore ??? to 5 Abundance
C — Seal it: No effect for now, inform control.
fields.Designer Notes: Surfaces Restorationist/Exploiter/Settler split.

entities.name: Engine Core Section

fields.Name: Engine Core Section
fields.Back Text:
You can start an exploration here by flipping and reading this card if you meet the requirements shown on the front.

The largest intact piece of the Aphelion — a battered ship fragment giving Engineering a true workshop and a direct telemetry feed from the reactor.

Flip-to-explore: 1 Oxygen + 3 Power.
fields.Front Text: The largest intact piece of the Aphelion — a battered ship fragment giving Engineering a true workshop and a direct telemetry feed from the reactor.
fields.Designer Notes: Mirrors PDF card 15 slot. Unlocks Thermal Power Generator recipe via the Hydrothermal keyword.

entities.name: Kelp Cathedral

fields.Name: Kelp Cathedral
fields.Back Text:
Your sonar maps a forest taller than the Aphelion was long.

Entry requirement: 2 [Oxygen icons]
fields.Front Text:
A cathedral of giant kelp pillars stretching from the seafloor to the limit of light. Cold, slow, vast.

Icons
1 [Oxygen icon]

Upkeep

Kelp: 1 biomass available per turn for crafting.

Rations: Each player here must either have a Food icon, reduce the population track of a flora by 1, or reduce the Rations Track by 1.
fields.Designer Notes: Standard Tier-2 location card.

entities.name: Giant Lungweed Stalks

fields.Name: Giant Lungweed Stalks
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Towering kelp that fills its hollow stalks with breathable air during the day.

Icons
Pop 2+: 1 [Oxygen icon]
Pop 3+: 1 [Pressure icon]

Triggers
Hush Mussels at Pop 3+ → +1 Pop/turn.
3 [Reactor icons]+ → -1 Pop/turn.
fields.Designer Notes: Tier-2 Pressure Rating source. No hand effect.

entities.name: Resonating Lure Fish

fields.Name: Resonating Lure Fish
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Long-bodied fish that drum sonic pulses into the kelp pillars to disorient prey.

Icons
Pop +2 and Prey 2+: 1 [Pressure icon]

Upkeep: 

Giant Lungweed Stalks at Pop 3+ → +1 Pop/turn.
No Flora here → -1 Pop/turn.
fields.Designer Notes: Mid-deck Fauna; pairs with Lungweed. No hand effect.

entities.name: Hush Mussels

fields.Name: Hush Mussels
fields.Back Text: Immediately draw this card and set its population track to 2.
fields.Front Text:
Filter feeders that cluster on the lower kelp. Damp acoustic noise in the cathedral.

Upkeep

Resonating Lure Fish at Pop 2+ → +1 Pop/turn.
No Mineral here → -1 Pop/turn.
fields.Designer Notes: Water source + cross-trigger with Lure Fish. No hand effect.

entities.name: Sunken Survey Drone

fields.Name: Sunken Survey Drone
fields.Back Text:
A pre-Aphelion survey drone tangled in the kelp. Still humming, still recording.

Put this card aside.

Upkeep
Spend 2 Materials to flip this card and set Scanning to 4.
fields.Front Text:
A pre-Aphelion survey drone tangled in the kelp. Still humming, still recording.

Icons
Scanning 3+ 1 [Knowledge icon]
Scanning 5+ +1 [Knowledge icon]

Upkeep
Add +1 Scanning

Can be moved between locations, if so reset scanning to 2.
fields.Designer Notes: Tier-2 Knowledge icon source. Wreckage keyword cross-deck nod. No hand effect.

entities.name: The Bloom

fields.Name: The Bloom
fields.Back Text:
Put this card aside.

Next time an exploration starts here flip this card.
fields.Front Text:
A current of nutrient-rich water sweeps through the cathedral. The whole place pulses.

All Kelp Flora in play here +1 Pop.
fields.Designer Notes: Standard depth-2 sequence-ender.

entities.name: Cathedral Hymn

fields.Name: Cathedral Hymn
fields.Back Text:
Italic tutorial: dual-prerequisite unlocks require two ecosystem cards at threshold simultaneously.


Set aside with this side up.

Gain when Giant Lungweed Stalks AND Resonating Lure Fish are both at Pop 5+ here.
fields.Front Text:
The kelp and the fish, together, are singing. 

Upkeep
+2 Pop to a fauna card if there is a kelp flora here.
fields.Designer Notes: Dual-prerequisite Knowledge per design.md §3.6.

entities.name: Echoing Drowned Mass

fields.Name: Echoing Drowned Mass
fields.Back Text:
Something hangs in the kelp at the edge of your light. It is the size of a man, and it has been there a long time.

Choose one unanimously:
A — Cut it free
B — Recover it
C — Document and leave
fields.Front Text:
Cut it free: ???
Recover it: ???
Document and leave: ???
fields.Designer Notes: First dilemma. Sets up the Drowned arc.

entities.name: Oxygen Tank

fields.Name: Oxygen Tank
fields.Back Text:
This is your first Aphelion Salvage recipe. Recipes live face-up at locations. Build during Upkeep by spending the listed resources at an outpost. The card then moves into your hand.

Upkeep
Spend 1 materials to take this card into your hand.
fields.Front Text:
Icon
1 [Oxygen icon]
fields.Designer Notes: Copies: 3. Simplest crafting tutorial.

Upkeep

fields.Front Text:
Icon
1 [Oxygen icon]

fields.Name: Field Welder
fields.Back Text:
Upkeep
Spend 2 materials to take this card into your hand.
fields.Front Text:
Icons
1 [Power Icon] if there is at least 2 [Oxygen icon]s
fields.Designer Notes: Copies: 3.

entities.name: Aphelion Scan Database

fields.Name: Aphelion Scan Database
fields.Back Text:
Upkeep
Requires: 3 [Power icons]
Take this card into your hand.
fields.Front Text:
Icons
1 [Knowledge Icon]

entities.name: Thermal Power Generator

fields.Name: Thermal Power Generator
fields.Back Text:
Upkeep
Spend 3 Materials to install this generator and flip this card. Cannot be moved once installed.
fields.Front Text:
Tucks under any outpost.

Icons
2 [Power icons]
fields.Designer Notes: Copies: 2. Cross-deck nudge to flip Engine Core Section in turn 1.

entities.name: The Aphelion Wraith

fields.Name: The Aphelion Wraith
fields.Back Text:
A long, silver shape moves through the deep at the edge of your sonar. It does not surface. It does not leave. The reef goes quiet.

During the upkeep phase choose 1, then flip this card.

Choose ONE response unanimously:
A — Drive it off (requires 2 [power icons])
B — Hide and wait
C — Observe and document
fields.Front Text:
Choose ONE response unanimously:
A — Drive it off: The Wraith leaves.
B — Hide and wait: spend nothing. All Fauna here lose 1 Pop.
C — Observe and document: All Fauna here lose 2 Pop.
fields.Designer Notes: Starting megafauna. Watcher in the Dark (Reef Cavern card 21) is the likely setup trigger. Option B is the philosophy trap.

entities.name: Reactor Pulse

fields.Name: Reactor Pulse
fields.Back Text: A pulse of warm, slightly acidic water washes through the shallows. Something deep below is leaking.
fields.Front Text: All Flora at every Tier-1 location lose 1 Population. All Mineral cards at every Tier-1 location lose 1 Abundance.
fields.Designer Notes: Global Tier-1 pressure cascade.

entities.name: Reactor Pulse

fields.Name: Reactor Pulse
fields.Back Text: A pulse of warm, slightly acidic water washes through the shallows. Something deep below is leaking.
fields.Front Text: All Flora at every Tier-1 location lose 1 Population. All Mineral cards at every Tier-1 location lose 1 Abundance.
fields.Designer Notes: Global Tier-1 pressure cascade.

entities.name: Lost Signal

fields.Name: Lost Signal
fields.Back Text:
On a frequency none of your equipment was tuned to, you pick up four seconds of voice. The language is not in any database. The cadence is unmistakable: it is a count. Counting down.

Talk to Control to start an expedition investigating the signal.
fields.Designer Notes: Pure narrative pressure per design.md §7.1.

fields.Text: Playtest configuration: 3 players, all Engineering, 2 turns.

entities.name: Original pacing 3

fields.Name: Original pacing 3
fields.Text:
TURN 1 (single shared expedition):
- All 3 players start at Crash Flats.
